# Introduction

Dodock Wolf is self-hosted observability for Frappe benches, ERPNext and Dokos sites and their
Linux hosts. It catches 502 windows, failed nightly crons, worker crashes and suspicious logins
before customers notice, and it keeps all data on a Frappe site you run.

:screenshot{alt="The Wolf UI overview on the demo bench" caption="The Wolf UI overview after the demo bench's 2AM scenario." name="overview"}

## Two parts

::card-group
  :::card
  ---
  icon: i-lucide-app-window
  title: Wolf App
  to: https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/wolf-app
  ---
  A Frappe app (`dodock_wolf`). It stores events, metrics, rules and incidents as DocTypes,
  evaluates alert rules at each scheduler tick and shows the timeline in the Wolf UI at `/wolf`
  and in Desk.
  :::

  :::card
  ---
  icon: i-lucide-server
  title: Wolf Agent
  to: https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/wolf-agent
  ---
  A Python daemon on each host, using only the standard library (Python 3.9 or later). It tails
  nginx, bench and auth logs, reads `/proc`, Redis, MariaDB and TLS certificates, and pushes
  batches over HTTPS.
  :::
::

The site running the Wolf App also watches itself, with no agent: failed scheduled jobs, Error
Logs, failed logins, privileged role grants and risky changes such as new Server Scripts. Other
sites on a bench can forward the same signals as [satellites](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/every-site).

## What it is for

| Signal                      | Example                                                                     | Where it comes from                                   |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| 5xx and 502 spikes          | 14 × 502 on `a.example.com` in 5 min, after a deployment at 01:47           | nginx access log (agent)                              |
| Cron and scheduler failures | The nightly job failed at 02:00, or the scheduler stalled                   | `scheduler.log` (agent), Scheduled Job Log (site)     |
| Worker problems             | Worker OOM-killed, RQ queue backlog, no live worker                         | `worker.log`, Redis (agent)                           |
| Host resources              | Disk at 93 % on `/`, load per core above 2                                  | `/proc` (agent)                                       |
| Security                    | SSH brute force, admin login from a new country, a web attack scan          | auth log, nginx (agent); login and audit hooks (site) |
| Operations                  | No backup for 26 h, TLS certificate expiring in 3 days, replication stopped | backups, TLS, MariaDB (agent)                         |

Every signal becomes a **Wolf Event** or a **Wolf Metric Sample**. **Wolf Alert Rules** turn them
into **Wolf Incidents**, which notify your channels when they open, reopen and resolve. See
[Concepts](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/getting-started/concepts).

## What it is not

Dodock Wolf is not a full Datadog replacement. It does no LLM observability, data observability,
real-user monitoring or SLO dashboards. It covers operational safety for Frappe (errors, cron,
workers, hosts) and the security signals around it, using open formats (JSON logs, syslog,
OCSF) and storage you own.

## Next

::card-group
  :::card
  ---
  icon: i-lucide-timer
  title: Quickstart
  to: https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/getting-started/quickstart
  ---
  From nothing to a first alert, on one bench.
  :::

  :::card
  ---
  icon: i-lucide-shapes
  title: Concepts
  to: https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/getting-started/concepts
  ---
  Events, metrics, rules, incidents and scopes.
  :::
::


# Quickstart

This guide sets up Dodock Wolf on one bench: the Wolf App on one site, the Wolf Agent on the
host, and an email alert for 502 spikes. Plan an afternoon.

**You need:** a Frappe 15 or Dokos (Dodock 5) bench, Node 20.19 or later for `bench build`, root on
the host, and a site that will hold Wolf's data (it can be an existing site).

::steps{level="3"}
### Install the Wolf App

```bash [bench]
cd ~/frappe-bench
bench get-app https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf
bench --site wolf.example.com install-app dodock_wolf
bench build --app dodock_wolf
```

Installing creates the roles **Wolf Manager** and **Wolf User**, a registration token and the
[preset alert rules](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/presets).

### Run the scheduler every minute

Wolf evaluates rules every minute, but Frappe 15 and Dodock tick every 4 minutes by default.

```bash [bench]
bench set-config -g scheduler_tick_interval 60
# then restart the bench's scheduler process (supervisor or systemd)
```

  :::warning
  Without this, an alert can come up to 4 minutes late, and "fire after 3 evaluations" means
  12 minutes. The Wolf UI's **Monitoring** page shows the pace in use.
  :::

### Install the agent on the host

Open **Wolf Settings → Agent install command** and copy the one-liner. It looks like this:

```bash [host]
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/main/agent/install.sh \
  | sudo WOLF_URL=https://wolf.example.com WOLF_TOKEN=<registration token> bash
```

The script installs the agent in `/opt/wolf-agent` (linked as `/usr/local/bin/wolf-agent`), creates a `wolf-agent` system user, registers the host, writes
`/etc/wolf-agent/config.json` and starts `wolf-agent.service`. It finds your benches by itself.

### Check what the agent sees

```bash [host]
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent discover
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent check --status
```

`discover` lists benches, sites and log paths. `check` collects once and prints the JSON it would
send, without sending it. `--status` also asks the site for its health.

### Add a channel to a rule

Presets open incidents but notify nobody until you add a channel. Open **Wolf Alert Rule → 502
spike after deployment**, add a row to **Channels** (type *Email*, your address), save, then
click **Send test notification**.

See [Channels](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/channels) for Slack, Raven, PagerDuty and the other types.

### Open the Wolf UI

Go to `https://wolf.example.com/wolf`. The overview lists hosts, benches and sites with their
latest metrics and open incidents. Within a minute of the first push, the host shows up.

To look at one moment, select a range on the **HTTP responses** chart: drag across it, or click
its first and last point (with the keyboard: arrow keys, then Enter twice). The chart, the
figures under **In this window** and the Events and Errors pages opened from them then cover
that range. The figures under **Now**, the signals and the list of hosts always show the present.
**Back to a relative window** returns to the last 24 hours.
::

## Mark your deployments

Rules such as *502 spike after deployment* only fire when a deployment hit the same scope recently.
Bench migrations on the Wolf site, and Press and Pilot tasks, are recorded by themselves. For other
benches, add one line to your deploy script:

```bash [deploy.sh]
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent mark-deployment --bench frappe-bench --note "v5.18.2" --silence 15m
```

The config holding the agent's secret is readable by `wolf-agent` only, hence `sudo -u`.
`--silence 15m` also opens a [maintenance window](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/rules#maintenance-windows): incidents
keep opening during the deploy, but their notifications wait until it ends.

## Next

- Watch the other sites of the bench: [Every site on a bench](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/every-site).
- Tune what the agent collects: [Configuration](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/configuration).
- Write your own rules: [Alert rules](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/rules).


# Concepts

## Scope: site, bench, host

Every record carries up to three names. Wolf always reads them in this order:

| Scope     | Is                                  | Example          |
| --------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| **site**  | a Frappe site                       | `erp.client.com` |
| **bench** | the bench that serves it            | `frappe-bench`   |
| **host**  | the Linux machine the agent runs on | `bench-01`       |

Host-wide records (CPU, disk, SSH logins) have no site. Rules group by one of these, and
[user scopes](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/access) restrict who sees which.

## From a log line to an alert

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  L[Log line, /proc, Redis] -->|agent| E[Wolf Event / Wolf Metric Sample]
  S[Site hooks] --> E
  E -->|rule, every minute| I[Wolf Incident]
  I -->|open, reopen, resolve| C[Channels]
```

1. The **agent** parses logs and reads system state. It sends events and metric samples every
   `push_interval` (30 s).
2. The **site** stores them. Events with the same fingerprint are counted on one row (**Count**,
   **Last Seen**) instead of piling up.
3. Every minute, each **alert rule** reads its window. When its condition holds, it opens an
   **incident** per group, or feeds the incident already open.
4. The incident notifies its **channels** when it opens, reopens, escalates and resolves, never
   on every event.

## The objects

| DocType                | What it holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Wolf Event**         | Something that happened: `error`, `cron_failure`, `worker_failure`, `security`, `host_metric_alert`, `deployment`. Has a category (for example `web_attack_probe`), a severity (`info`, `warning`, `critical`), a scope, a count and a JSON payload. |
| **Wolf Metric Sample** | One value of one metric (`cpu_usage`, `http_502`, `tls_days_left`…) for one scope at one time. Rolled up into **Wolf Metric Rollup** by minute and by hour. See [Metric storage](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/metric-storage).    |
| **Wolf Alert Rule**    | *When X > Y for Z minutes, send alert.* Signal, aggregation, window, group by, channels. See [Alert rules](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/rules).                                                                                      |
| **Wolf Incident**      | Events that share a cause, for one group of one rule. Status `Open`, `Acknowledged` or `Resolved`. Linked to the deployment that preceded it. See [Incidents](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/incidents).                               |
| **Wolf Silence**       | A maintenance window: incidents still open, notifications wait.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Wolf Agent**         | One registered host, satellite site or integration, with its last push and clock skew.                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Wolf Settings**      | Retention, signals, agents, SIEM export, threat intelligence.                                                                                                                                                                                        |

## Severity

Each severity has a colour and a shape, so it never depends on colour alone:

| Severity   | Glyph | Meaning                           |
| ---------- | ----- | --------------------------------- |
| `info`     | ○     | Worth knowing. Digest-friendly.   |
| `warning`  | ◐     | Look at it today.                 |
| `critical` | ●     | Someone wakes up. Never digested. |
| resolved   | ✓     | Back to normal.                   |

## Deployments

A `deployment` event marks the moment code changed: a `bench migrate` on the Wolf site, a Press or
Pilot task, or `wolf-agent mark-deployment`. Rules can require a recent deployment (the
*502 spike after deployment* preset), and incidents show the deployment that preceded them, so the
timeline reads "502s started 4 minutes after the 01:47 deploy".

## Where to look

- **Wolf UI** at `/wolf`: overview, incidents, explorers, metrics, security, monitoring. For Wolf
  Users and Wolf Managers.
- **Desk**: every DocType, configuration, reports such as **Wolf Incident Metrics**.


# Wolf App

The Wolf App (`dodock_wolf`) runs on a Frappe or Dokos site. That site becomes the **central** Wolf
site: agents push to it, rules run on it, and the Wolf UI is served from it at `/wolf`.

## Requirements

- Frappe 15 or Dokos (Dodock 5). Tested on Dodock 5.18, MariaDB 10.6 and Postgres 16 and 17.
- Node 20.19 or later on the bench, for `bench build` of the Wolf UI.
- A scheduler running every minute (below).

## Install

```bash [bench]
cd ~/frappe-bench
bench get-app https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf
bench --site wolf.example.com install-app dodock_wolf
bench build --app dodock_wolf   # links the static assets and builds the Wolf UI (/wolf)
bench set-config -g scheduler_tick_interval 60
```

Then restart the scheduler process.

Installing creates:

- the roles **Wolf Manager** (sees and configures everything) and **Wolf User** (read-only);
- a random **registration token** in **Wolf Settings**, used by agents to register;
- the [preset alert rules](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/presets), with no channels.

## Scheduler pace

Wolf's alert rules, rollups and satellite pushes are scheduled every minute. Frappe 15 and Dodock
tick every 4 minutes by default.

::warning
Without `scheduler_tick_interval` set to `60`, an alert can come up to 4 minutes late, and "fire
after 3 evaluations" means 12 minutes. The Wolf UI's **Monitoring** page shows the pace in use.
::

## The Wolf UI

`https://<site>/wolf` is the operator UI, a Vue app built on frappe-ui. It reuses the Frappe
session: guests go to the login page, users without **Wolf User** or **Wolf Manager** get a 403.
Desk keeps the configuration DocTypes; a view the Wolf UI does not have yet links to Desk.

:screenshot{alt="An incident in the Wolf UI" caption="An incident: timeline, deployment marker, and the events grouped under it." name="incident"}

## Signals with no agent

The Wolf site watches itself as soon as the app is installed: failed Scheduled Job Logs, Error Logs
and failed backups, failed desk logins, privileged logins from a new IP or country, role grants,
Email Queue backlogs and risky application changes. Each can be turned off in **Wolf Settings**.
See [Site signals](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/site-signals).

To get the same signals from the bench's other sites, install the app there too, as
[satellites](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/every-site).

## Upgrade

```bash [bench]
bench update --apps dodock_wolf   # or: cd apps/dodock_wolf && git pull
bench --site wolf.example.com migrate
bench build --app dodock_wolf
```

Migrations never overwrite presets you edited. A `bench migrate` is recorded as a deployment on
the Wolf timeline.

## Next

[Install the agent](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/wolf-agent) on each host.


# Wolf Agent

The Wolf Agent is a Python daemon (3.9 or later, standard library only). Install one per host:
it watches every bench on that host.

## One-line install

Copy the command from **Wolf Settings → Agent install command**, or write it yourself:

```bash [host]
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/main/agent/install.sh \
  | sudo WOLF_URL=https://wolf.example.com WOLF_TOKEN=<registration token> bash
```

From a checkout of the repository:

```bash [host]
sudo WOLF_URL=https://wolf.example.com WOLF_TOKEN=<registration token> ./agent/install.sh
```

The script:

1. creates a venv in `/opt/wolf-agent` and links `/usr/local/bin/wolf-agent`;
2. creates the system user `wolf-agent` and adds it to `adm`, `systemd-journal` and `frappe` when
   those groups exist, so it reads auth, nginx and bench logs without root;
3. registers the host and writes `/etc/wolf-agent/config.json` (mode 0600);
4. installs and starts `wolf-agent.service`;
5. on a [Frappe Pilot](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/pilot) host, installs `wolf-pilot-export`, a root timer that copies
   the bench's task and process states the agent cannot read itself.

## Install options

| Variable          | Effect                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WOLF_URL`        | The central Wolf site.                                                                                               |
| `WOLF_TOKEN`      | Its registration token (**Wolf Settings**).                                                                          |
| `WOLF_BENCHES`    | Space-separated bench paths, to skip auto-discovery: `"/home/frappe/frappe-bench /srv/other-bench"`.                 |
| `WOLF_AGENT_SRC`  | pip source: a local directory or a `git+https` URL. Default: the script's directory, or GitHub when piped from curl. |
| `WOLF_AGENT_REF`  | Git ref when installing from GitHub. Default `main`.                                                                 |
| `WOLF_INSECURE=1` | Skip TLS verification during registration and pushes (self-signed Wolf site).                                        |

Without `WOLF_URL` and `WOLF_TOKEN`, the agent is installed but not registered. Register it later:

```bash [host]
sudo wolf-agent --config /etc/wolf-agent/config.json register --url https://wolf.example.com --token <token>
sudo chown wolf-agent: /etc/wolf-agent/config.json && sudo systemctl start wolf-agent
```

Without systemd (a container), the script prints the command to run as `wolf-agent`.

## Bench discovery

The agent finds benches by itself:

- a `bench.toml`, or a directory with `sites/` and `apps/frappe`;
- [Pilot benches](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/pilot), read with Pilot's real `bench.toml` schema;
- [Press servers](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/press), detected from `/home/frappe/agent/config.json`.

```bash [host]
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent discover
```

## Check it

```bash [host]
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent doctor           # what this host gives the agent, and what to fix
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent check            # collect once, print the payload, send nothing
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent check --status   # also ask the site for its health
journalctl -u wolf-agent -f
```

Within a minute the host appears in the Wolf UI. On the Wolf site it is a **Wolf Agent** record
(`WAG-0001`…) carrying its host name.

## Credentials

The agent's secret is shown once, at registration. The site keeps only a salted HMAC-SHA256 hash.
To move an agent or recover a lost config, click **Rotate secret** on the **Wolf Agent** form, or
register the host again.

If the site rejects the credentials (401 or 403), the agent sends a last [watchdog](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/watchdog)
alert and exits with status 2, and systemd stops restarting it.

## Next

- [What is collected](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/collected)
- [Configuration](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/configuration)


# Every site on a bench

Some signals can only be seen from inside a site. Frappe logs "Scheduled Job Failed" at INFO, which
the default logger level drops, and it often writes no Scheduled Job Log. So the agent cannot see a
failing cron on a site from `scheduler.log`.

Install `dodock_wolf` on every site. Keep one **central** Wolf site, and set the others to
**satellite** mode.

## Register a satellite

```bash [bench]
bench --site b.example.com install-app dodock_wolf
bench --site b.example.com execute dodock_wolf.satellite.register \
  --kwargs '{"url": "https://wolf.example.com", "token": "<central registration token>"}'
```

Add `"verify_tls": 0` to the kwargs for a self-signed central site.

In Desk: **Wolf Settings → Register with central site**.

## What a satellite does

- It captures its local signals, with the same **Wolf Settings** switches: failed scheduled jobs,
  Error Logs and failed backups, logins (including new IPs and countries), privileged role grants,
  Email Queue backlog and errors, and `bench migrate`.
- It stores them in **Wolf Outbox** and pushes them every minute to the central site through the
  agent ingest API, with the same host, bench and site scope. Central rules and incidents see them
  like any other event.
- While the central site is unreachable, it retries with backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, then every 15
  minutes) and keeps at most 10,000 pending events, dropping the oldest.
- It shows the forwarding status on **Wolf Overview** and **Wolf Settings**. **Forward now** pushes
  at once.
- It evaluates no rules, opens no incidents and stores no Wolf Events.

## On the central site

The satellite is a **Wolf Agent** of kind `satellite`, named after its site. It pushes every minute
even with nothing to send, so the **Agent silent** preset also fires when a satellite's scheduler
stops.

- Disable the Wolf Agent to stop accepting its events.
- Set **Mode** back to `central` on the satellite to make it a standalone Wolf again.
- The satellite keeps its secret encrypted in its Wolf Settings, since it has to send it. The
  central site stores only the hash.


# Press servers

[Press](https://github.com/frappe/press){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} is the Frappe app behind Frappe Cloud. It manages servers through the **Press agent** ([frappe/agent](https://github.com/frappe/agent){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}), a Flask + RQ service on each server. This page covers the Wolf Agent on an *app server* managed that way.

::note
This is for **self-hosted Press** deployments, where you control the server. Frappe Cloud's hosted servers are not open to customers.
::

Everything on this page was checked on a Press app server set up by **Press's own Ansible roles** (frappe/press [`7ce25f2`](https://github.com/frappe/press/tree/7ce25f221378cb4558cd3993f3283d75cc8fe7d7){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, frappe/agent [`6bbd199`](https://github.com/frappe/agent/tree/6bbd199c13e90f48950e2a06401ca98738455aaf){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, November 2026), with benches and sites created through the Press agent's API as Press creates them, and real deploys: New Bench, Update Site Migrate, Bench Restart, Archive Bench and failed jobs. The repository's [`dev/press`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/tree/main/dev/press){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} sets the same server up in a container.

::tip
No Press server at hand? `dev/press` above, or the [Press demo](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/development), which simulates one for the Wolf Agent to read.
::

## Install

Install the agent as on any host ([Wolf Agent](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/wolf-agent)). Press mode needs no extra step and no Press credentials: everything is read from local files.

::steps{level="3"}
### Let detection run

The agent switches to Press mode when `/home/frappe/agent/config.json` exists with a `benches_directory` key. The daemon's own user cannot read that file (mode `0600`): there, the file and `jobs.sqlite3` being present is enough. Registration runs as root and also saves `"platform": "press"` and the benches folder in Wolf's config. In Press mode, the `benches` list in the config is refreshed from disk at start and on every rediscovery.

### Check what Wolf finds

```bash
wolf-agent discover --platform press
```

`discover` shows what bench discovery finds. `wolf-agent register --platform press` records the Press layout in the config.

### Check what would be sent

```bash
wolf-agent check --platform press
```

`check` collects once and prints the JSON payload. Nothing is sent. See [Commands](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/commands).
::

### Configuration

Press mode is auto-detected. To force it, or to change the paths, edit `/etc/wolf-agent/config.json`:

```json [config.json]
{
  "platform": "press",
  "press": {
    "agent_dir": "/home/frappe/agent",
    "nginx_access_log": "/var/log/nginx/access.log",
    "rediscover_interval": 60,
    "deployments": true
  }
}
```

::field-group
  :::field{name="platform" type="string | null"}
  `null` auto-detects Press, `"press"` forces it, `"generic"` disables Press handling.
  :::

  :::field{name="press.agent_dir" type="string"}
  Press agent directory. Default `/home/frappe/agent`.
  :::

  :::field{name="press.benches_directory" type="string | null"}
  The Press agent's `benches_directory`, saved by registration, which reads it as root. Used when the daemon cannot read the Press agent's config. Default `/home/frappe/benches`.
  :::

  :::field{name="press.nginx_access_log" type="string"}
  Shared nginx access log. Default `/var/log/nginx/access.log`.
  :::

  :::field{name="press.rediscover_interval" type="number"}
  Seconds between bench rescans. Default `60`.
  :::

  :::field{name="press.deployments" type="boolean"}
  Turn Press agent jobs into `deployment` events. Default `true`.
  :::

  :::field{name="backups.press" type="boolean"}
  Read Press benches' backups from their `sites/<site>/private/backups` folder, as on other benches. Default `false`: from the Press agent's Backup Site jobs.
  :::
::

The full config is on [Configuration](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/configuration).

### Permissions

`install.sh` adds the `wolf-agent` user to the `frappe` and `adm` groups. On a server set up by Press's roles, that gives it:

| File                                                             | Mode                 | `wolf-agent`          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------- |
| `/home/frappe`                                                   | `0750 frappe:frappe` | enters (group)        |
| `<bench>/logs/*`                                                 | `0644`               | reads                 |
| `jobs.sqlite3`, `-wal`, `-shm`                                   | `0644`               | reads, with `mode=ro` |
| `/var/log/nginx/access.log`                                      | `0640 www-data:adm`  | reads (group `adm`)   |
| `<bench>/docker-compose.yml`, `<bench>/nginx.conf`               | `0644`               | reads                 |
| `/home/frappe/agent/config.json`                                 | `0600`               | no                    |
| `<bench>/config.json`                                            | `0600`               | no                    |
| `sites/common_site_config.json`, `sites/<site>/site_config.json` | `0600`               | no                    |

The Press agent writes its configs `0600`, so the daemon reads them only through registration, which runs as root. At run time a new bench is found from the files it can read: its image from `docker-compose.yml`; its web port, sites and custom domains from its `nginx.conf`; and its `rq_port` from that web port, since Press gives a bench one offset for all its ports (`web_port` 18000 + offset, `rq_port` 11000 + offset).

## What Wolf does on a Press server

| Area               | What Wolf does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Status                                                 |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Detection          | Press mode turns on when `/home/frappe/agent/config.json` has a `benches_directory` key, when it is there next to `jobs.sqlite3` (unreadable), or when `"platform": "press"` is set                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | checked                                                |
| Benches            | Lists `<benches_directory>/*` that have a `sites/` directory and `config.json` with a `docker_image`, or, unreadable, `config.json` next to a `docker-compose.yml`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | checked                                                |
| Rediscovery        | Rescans every `press.rediscover_interval` seconds (default 60), because each deploy creates a new bench directory                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | checked: a new bench is tailed within a minute         |
| Bench logs         | Tails `<bench>/logs/*` (bind-mounted from the container) and `sites/<site>/logs/*`, with the same parsers as other benches                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | done                                                   |
| nginx              | Tails `/var/log/nginx/access.log` (Press's `main` format, which logs `$host`) and maps custom domains to sites                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | done, unit tested                                      |
| Redis queue        | Reads `queue_length`, the RQ failed/started registries, live workers and Redis memory/evictions from `redis://127.0.0.1:<rq_port>` (bench `config.json`, or 11000 + the bench's port offset)                                                                                                                                                                                                              | checked                                                |
| TLS expiry         | Checks every site and custom domain like on other benches. Certificates live on the proxy server, so the public handshake measures what customers see                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | done (generic)                                         |
| Backups            | From the Press agent's job history: `backup_age_hours` per site from its newest successful **Backup Site** job, and a `backup_failed` event (critical, the *Backup failed* preset) when one fails. Press deletes offsite backups from the server after the upload, or streams them, so the backups folder says nothing. `backups.press: true` reads the folder instead                                    | checked                                                |
| Processes          | **Skipped**: supervisor runs inside each bench container and Wolf never runs `docker`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | —                                                      |
| MariaDB            | Not on Press: the site's database password is in its `site_config.json`, readable by `frappe` only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | —                                                      |
| Site config risks  | `developer_mode`, `allow_tests`… need the `0600` site configs: no sample, shown as unknown                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | checked                                                |
| Exposed services   | The Press agent publishes each bench's queue and cache Redis on all interfaces (`-p 0.0.0.0:<rq_port>:11000`, `<rq_cache_port>:13000`), for secondary servers. Wolf reports them as `service_exposed`: Press relies on the server's firewall to keep them private                                                                                                                                         | checked                                                |
| Proxy server       | The Wolf Agent on a Press proxy reads its access log, each line's site from `$host`. A web client is blocked there: the app server behind it proposes blocks for SSH only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | checked                                                |
| Deploy correlation | A `deployment` event for each deploy, update or migrate job in the Press agent's `jobs.sqlite3`, and an `error` event when one fails                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | checked                                                |
| Site events        | The Wolf App on a Press bench names its bench and server as the agent does: the container's hostname is the bench (`docker run --hostname <bench>`), and Press's `supervisor.conf` names the server (`<server>-gunicorn.access.log`, its name in Press). Registration names the agent's host the same way, from the Press agent's config, unless `--hostname` is given or the agent was registered before | checked (the test server's hostname is its Press name) |
| Fallback           | If `jobs.sqlite3` cannot be read, a `deployment` event when a new bench appears or a site moves to another bench                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | done, unit tested                                      |

The metrics themselves are described on [What is collected](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/collected).

## Server layout

### Press agent directory

Ansible clones the Press agent into `/home/frappe/agent/repo`, creates a venv at `/home/frappe/agent/env`, and runs `agent setup config` and `agent setup database` from `/home/frappe/agent`. `agent setup config` writes `config.json` with `benches_directory: /home/<user>/benches`, `nginx_directory: /home/<user>/agent/nginx`, `redis_port: 25025`, `web_port: 25052`, and other keys. Wolf detects Press through this file and its `benches_directory` key.

### Benches

Each bench is `<benches_directory>/<name>/` with `logs/`, `sites/`, `config/` and a bench `config.json`. Bench names follow the pattern `bench-<candidate>-<server>`. Wolf uses the directory name.

The apps live **inside the Docker image**. There is no `apps/frappe` on the host, so Wolf's generic check (`sites/` + `apps/frappe`) misses Press benches. A Press bench is identified by `config.json` with a `docker_image` key.

Bench config keys come from Press's `Bench` doctype: `docker_image`, `web_port` (18000 + offset), `socketio_port`, `rq_port` (11000 + offset), `rq_cache_port`, `single_container: true`, and others.

The bench containers bind-mount `<bench>/sites` and `<bench>/logs`, whether the bench runs as a single container or through `docker stack deploy`. The bench logs are ordinary files on the host. Wolf never runs `docker`.

### Sites and custom domains

Sites are `sites/<site>/` directories with a `site_config.json`. A site's custom domains are listed in its `site_config.json` under `domains`, and the bench nginx config maps them back to the site. Wolf reads the same key, so a 502 logged for `erp.customer.com` is counted against the right site.

### Logs

Inside the container, supervisor writes these files into `logs/`:

- `web.log`, `web.error.log`
- `schedule.log`, `schedule.error.log`
- `worker.log`, `worker.error.log`

Frappe's own loggers write `frappe.web.log`, `scheduler.log` and the other files there as on any bench. Wolf also tails `schedule.error.log` for tracebacks, on every bench. Where nothing writes it, the file is simply absent.

### Redis queue

`sites/common_site_config.json` holds the **in-container** address `redis://localhost:11000`. From the host, the queue Redis is reachable on the published `rq_port`, which is where the Press agent's own RQ exporter connects. Wolf uses `redis://127.0.0.1:<rq_port>`. When a bench has no `rq_port`, Wolf skips its queue metrics.

### nginx

The root `nginx.conf` is rendered to `/home/frappe/agent/nginx/nginx.conf`, symlinked to `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf`, and includes every `<benches_directory>/*/nginx.conf`. Every vhost uses one log:

```nginx
log_format main '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" $status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" "$http_user_agent" "$http_x_forwarded_for" "$host" $request_time';
access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;
```

The site name, or a custom domain, is the last quoted field `"$host"`. Wolf's nginx parser reads trailing quoted fields, and Press mode adds the domain → site map. The bench templates set no per-bench `access_log`. Behind a Press proxy, `$remote_addr` is still the client: the app server's nginx takes it from the proxy's `X-Real-IP` (`set_real_ip_from <proxy_ip>`, set by `agent setup config --proxy-ip`).

### Proxy servers

A Press proxy server (an `n*` host) terminates TLS for the sites of its app servers and forwards them to port 80, with the client in `X-Real-IP`. Install the Wolf Agent there too:

- Registration recognises a proxy by the Press agent's `nginx/proxy.conf` (Press's `proxy` role creates it) and adds its `/var/log/nginx/access.log` to `extra_logs` with `"site_from_host": true`. A line's site is its `$host`. A custom domain maps to its site through the proxy's `nginx/hosts/<domain>/map.json` (Add Host to Proxy). The proxy's own name, its Press agent's vhost, is no site.
- Its web events land in the same incidents as the app server's, under the same site.
- **Blocking a web client works on the proxy, not on the app server.** On the app server, the client's packets come from the proxy, so a block there would stop nothing. The app server's agent reports its proxy (`proxy_ip` from the Press agent's config, saved by registration). For that host, the Wolf site proposes blocks for SSH events only, and lists the web clients it did not propose there with the reason. The proxy's agent proposes the blocks that take effect. See [Response actions](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/response-actions).

The Press agent writes each site's TLS key (`nginx/hosts/<domain>/privkey.pem`) mode `0644` under `/home/frappe` (`0750`): the `frappe` group, the Wolf Agent's user included, can read them. Wolf never reads them.

## Deployment events

### Job history

Every Press agent job is stored in the SQLite database `jobs.sqlite3`, in the agent's working directory (`/home/frappe/agent`). It runs in WAL mode. Two tables matter:

- `jobmodel(id, name, status ∈ Pending/Running/Success/Failure, agent_job_id, data, enqueue, start, end, duration)`
- `stepmodel(id, name, job_id, status, data, start, end, duration)`

`agent_job_id` is the name of the **Agent Job** document in Press. Wolf copies it into the event payload, so you can open the same job in the Press dashboard.

At enqueue time, `data` is `{"function", "args", "kwargs"}`. When the job ends, it is overwritten with the result or `{"traceback": …}`. Step `data` keeps each step's command result, including the `docker exec … <bench> bench --site <site> …` command line.

Timestamps are naive server local time. Wolf converts them to UTC as local time.

### Jobs treated as deployments

| Press agent job                                                           | Bench / site taken from                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| New Bench                                                                 | `args[0]` (bench)                      |
| Update Site Pull, Update Site Migrate                                     | `args[0]` site, `args[2]` target bench |
| Recover Failed Site Migrate, Recover Failed Site Pull, Move Site to Bench | `args[0]` site, `args[2]` target bench |
| Recover Failed Site Update                                                | `args[0]` site, `args[1]` bench        |
| Update Bench In Place                                                     | `args[0]` sites; bench from steps      |
| Patch App, Bench Restart, Rebuild Bench Assets                            | steps                                  |
| Migrate Site, Install App on Site, Uninstall App on Site                  | steps                                  |

`Bench` and `Site` methods carry no bench or site name in their arguments. For those jobs, Wolf searches the job and step `data` for a known bench name and for `--site <name>`.

### How events are produced

- **Read-only access, creating no file.** Wolf opens `jobs.sqlite3` with `file:…?mode=ro` while the Press agent's `-wal` and `-shm` files are there, else with `immutable=1`. A reader creates them when they are missing (after the Press agent's last connection closed), the agent's folder is writable by the `frappe` group, and files Wolf created would leave the Press agent unable to write its own database. Wolf never writes to the database.
- **One `deployment` event per job**, sent as soon as the job has started. Its timestamp is the job's `start`, so the "502 spike after deployment" [preset](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/presets) links incidents that happen during a long migrate. If the bench cannot be determined yet, the event waits up to 2 minutes for a step to name it, then ships host-scoped. Incident correlation also matches host-scoped deployments. Fields: `category: "press"`, `source: "press-agent"`, and `payload.press_job`, `agent_job_id`, `local_job_id`, `sites`.
- **One `backup_failed` event per failed Backup Site job** (an `error`, critical, the *Backup failed* preset), read apart from the deployment jobs: the backups Press queues for every site at once never hold a deployment event back, and the first poll after an install or an upgrade replays no old failure. Successful Backup Site jobs, local, offsite or streamed, give the sites' `backup_age_hours`.
- **One `error` event** (`category: "press_job_failed"`, warning) when such a job ends in `Failure`. Its payload holds the failed step names and the tail of the traceback or output.
- **Deduplication.** Emitted job ids and a floor id are saved in `<spool_dir>/press-jobs.json`, so restarts never emit an event twice. On the first run, history is skipped and only jobs still Pending or Running are picked up. A job stuck in Pending or Running for more than 24 h (for example, a crashed RQ worker) is dropped, so it cannot block progress.
- **Fallback without database access.** `<spool_dir>/press-benches.json` keeps a bench → site snapshot. A new bench directory, or a site whose directory moved to another bench, produces a `deployment` event stamped with the time it was noticed.

Rediscovery rebuilds the log sources when the set of benches or sites changes. Logs of a bench created while Wolf runs are read from the start, because they are new files. A moved site's logs move with its directory, so they are read from the end to avoid replaying them.

Event fields are described in the [protocol](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/protocol).

## Wolf next to Press's own monitoring

Press already ships a monitoring stack. Wolf does not replace it and does not touch it.

- **Monitor server** (`monitor.yml`): Prometheus, Alertmanager, Blackbox exporter and Grafana. Prometheus probes sites, domains and TLS with blackbox `http_2xx` and scrapes the Press-managed servers. Press pushes alert rules and routes to it through the agent's `Monitor` class, from Press doctypes such as *Prometheus Alert Rule*. The Alertmanager webhook lands in *Alertmanager Webhook Log*. Press's *Incident* doctype escalates outages by phone (Twilio) to Frappe staff and customers.
- **App servers** (`server.yml`): node_exporter, cAdvisor, statsd_exporter (the bench config sets `statsd_host`), filebeat and fail2ban, among other roles. Filebeat ships `/var/log/*.log`, the nginx module and each bench's `logs/monitor.json.log` to a central Elasticsearch/Kibana log server. The Press agent also moves `monitor.json.log` aside for Press's analytics. Wolf does not tail that file.
- The Press agent exposes RQ metrics per bench at `/benches/metrics`.

What Wolf adds on a self-hosted Press install:

- Frappe-level tracebacks, failed scheduled jobs and worker crashes read from bench logs.
- 5xx/502 per site.
- SSH signals.
- Incidents correlated with the Press job that caused them.

All of it lives on your own Wolf site, without access to the Press monitor server.

The two stacks overlap on host metrics (node_exporter vs Wolf's `/proc` sampling) and on queue lengths. Wolf's are light. Turn host metrics off with `collect_host_metrics: false`.

## Limitations and unverified points

### Limitations

- App servers with benches and proxy servers are supported directly ([Proxy servers](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#proxy-servers)). Database servers have no bench: add their logs through `extra_logs`.
- When a job ends, the Press agent replaces its arguments with its result. A job Wolf first sees finished takes the bench its last step ran in (a site move ends on its target) and the site from `--site` in a step command. A job without any such step is reported host-scoped.
- The filesystem fallback cannot tell a deploy from a manual move, and it has no failure signal.
- A bench found after registration shows the image it was created with (its `docker-compose.yml`): Update Bench In Place changes only its `0600` config.
- Jobs are matched by display name. If Press renames a job, it is no longer recognised. Add the new name to `DEPLOY_JOBS` in [`agent/wolf_agent/press.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/agent/wolf_agent/press.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.
- An auto-scaling **secondary** app server runs the primary's benches from an NFS mount, its containers writing to the same bench logs: Wolf Agents on both would read those logs twice. Not checked: install the Wolf Agent on the primary only.

### Checked on a Press server

1. **Modes.** `jobs.sqlite3` and its `-wal` and `-shm` files are `0644`, and `mode=ro` works for a member of the `frappe` group. The configs are `0600`: see [Permissions](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#permissions).
2. **Job data.** Job names match `DEPLOY_JOBS`. A finished job's `data` is `null`, and its steps keep their command and `directory`, for example `docker exec … bench-0001-000002-f1 bench --site <site> migrate` for a migrate.
3. **`$host`.** Every site request carries the site in `"$host"`. The Press agent's own vhost on 443 logs the server's name there, which is no site: Wolf leaves those lines out.
4. **`rq_port`.** Press sets it on every new bench and publishes it. A bench whose config has none (an older one) gets no queue metrics: the daemon keeps what registration read in it rather than derive a port from the web port.
5. **Behind a proxy server.** Through Press's proxy (its own `proxy` role and Add Upstream / Add Host / Add Site to Upstream jobs), the app server's `access.log` keeps the real client in `$remote_addr`, and the site sees it in its failed logins. A block applied on the app server stopped nothing, the one on the proxy did: hence [Proxy servers](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#proxy-servers).
6. **Backups.** A local-only Backup Site job leaves its files in `sites/<site>/private/backups` and lists them in its result. An offsite one deletes them after the upload (`upload_offsite_backup`) unless the server keeps them, and a streamed one writes none. Wolf reads the job history: a backup and a failed one (the database server stopped) both came through.
7. **Shared FS** (Run Benches on Shared FS, primary server). Press's `link_benches_to_nfs` role makes `/home/frappe/shared` a link to `/home/frappe/benches`, and the job points `benches_directory` at it and restarts the benches. Wolf kept reading the same benches through its saved folder, jobs stayed scoped (Wolf compares the folders with links resolved, so a New Bench there is scoped before the next `wolf-agent refresh`), and `refresh` saved the new folder. Bench paths are resolved, so each log keeps its read position across the switch.

Not checked: an auto-scaling secondary server (see [Limitations](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#limitations)).

- Step command lines: [`agent/base.py#L65-L111`](https://github.com/frappe/agent/blob/64b9812a8e4dc82188d3cbf3053dd4f2eb5f4f4a/agent/base.py#L65-L111){rel=""nofollow""}, [`agent/bench.py#L177-L200`](https://github.com/frappe/agent/blob/64b9812a8e4dc82188d3cbf3053dd4f2eb5f4f4a/agent/bench.py#L177-L200){rel=""nofollow""}, [`agent/site.py#L61-L62`](https://github.com/frappe/agent/blob/64b9812a8e4dc82188d3cbf3053dd4f2eb5f4f4a/agent/site.py#L61-L62){rel=""nofollow""}

**Jobs treated as deployments**

::


# Pilot benches

[Pilot](https://github.com/frappe/pilot){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} is **Frappe's** server manager ("Frappe Server Manager"). It is not a Dokos tool: Dokos' public GitLab group has no Pilot repository. The Dokos documentation mentions Pilot only through the `pilot_endpoint` / `pilot_auth_token` site keys used by the Cloud Settings panel for Frappe Cloud v2 sites. These are the same keys Pilot writes into `site_config.json`.

Everything on this page was checked on a live Pilot host: **Pilot v1.0.0-rc.1**, and again on **v1.0.0-rc.2** (which changes only Pilot's release CI), in production mode (systemd user units, nginx, the Admin), a Frappe 16 bench and a site running the Wolf App. The repository's [`dev/pilot`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/tree/main/dev/pilot){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} sets the same host up in a container.

## Install

Install the agent as on any host ([Wolf Agent](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/wolf-agent)). It runs as its own `wolf-agent` user, out of the bench's reach: code that takes over a Frappe site cannot read its config, its integrity key or its state, nor stop it.

Pilot keeps a bench's `bench.toml`, its `tasks/` and its site configs readable by the bench user only, and runs the bench as that user's systemd user units, which another user cannot list. So on a Pilot host the installer also sets up **`wolf-pilot-export`**, a root helper run by `wolf-pilot-export.timer` every 20 seconds. It writes `/var/lib/wolf-pilot-export/<bench>.json` (`root:wolf-agent`, mode `0640`, in a folder root owns) with:

- the latest 100 tasks: command, status, times, exit code, failure code and message, and of the arguments only the site;
- the state of the bench's `<bench>-*.service` user units.

It reads the bench's files as the bench user, in a child process with a time limit: a link that user plants there gives access to nothing more than they could already read. It takes a bench only when its `[bench] name` is its folder's name and the folder belongs to the user whose home holds it. It copies nothing else: not `bench.toml` (its Admin secret), not the site configs (their database passwords). Registration runs as root, so discovery still reads `bench.toml` and the site configs once, for the bench's name, sites, domains and ports.

What this costs on Pilot: the [MariaDB checks](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/collected), which need a site's database password.

To remove Wolf from a Pilot host, run `systemctl disable --now wolf-pilot-export.timer` before deleting the `wolf-agent` user: the helper's unit runs with that group, and fails at every run without it.

::steps{level="3"}
### Check what Wolf finds

```bash
sudo wolf-agent discover
```

### Check what would be sent

```bash
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent --config /etc/wolf-agent/config.json check
```

`check` collects once and prints the JSON payload. Nothing is sent. See [Commands](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/commands).
::

::warning
Worker log names are globbed at registration. Re-run `wolf-agent register` after changing `[[workers]]` in `bench.toml`.
::

### Configuration

Deployment events from Pilot tasks are on by default. The `pilot` section of `/etc/wolf-agent/config.json`:

```json [config.json]
{
  "pilot": {
    "deployments": true,
    "api_url": null,
    "token": null,
    "jwt_secret": null
  }
}
```

::field-group
  :::field{name="pilot.deployments" type="boolean"}
  Poll Pilot tasks and turn them into events. `false` turns task polling off. Default `true`.
  :::

  :::field{name="pilot.api_url" type="string | null"}
  Overrides the per-bench Admin API address `http://127.0.0.1:<admin.port+1>`. It applies to every Pilot bench on the host, so set it only on single-bench hosts.
  :::

  :::field{name="pilot.token" type="string | null"}
  A bench-scoped Admin API token, used only without `wolf-pilot-export`'s copy.
  :::

  :::field{name="pilot.jwt_secret" type="string | null"}
  The bench's `[admin] jwt_secret`, to mint a one-hour token, only without `wolf-pilot-export`'s copy.
  :::
::

With `wolf-pilot-export`, Wolf needs neither. The full config is on [Configuration](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/configuration).

## What Wolf does on a Pilot bench

| Area                                         | What Wolf does                                                                                                                                                                                                 | On v1.0.0-rc.1 and rc.2                           |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Discovery                                    | Searches `/home/*/pilot/benches/*`. A `bench.toml` with `[bench] name` and `python` is a Pilot bench, read with its real keys                                                                                  | checked                                           |
| Sites                                        | Reads `sites/*/site_config.json`, plus `domains` (plain strings or `{"domain": …, "route": …}`) for host → site mapping                                                                                        | checked                                           |
| Process logs                                 | Tails `web` and its stderr file, and the worker and schedule logs of a bench out of lite mode. On a sandboxed bench, Frappe's own logs in `logs/workload/`                                                     | checked (lite mode); `logs/workload/` unit tested |
| nginx                                        | Tails `<bench>/logs/nginx-access.log`, in the `pilot_access` format                                                                                                                                            | checked                                           |
| Redis queue                                  | Queue length, RQ registries, workers and Redis memory from `[redis] queue_port`                                                                                                                                | checked                                           |
| MariaDB                                      | Not on Pilot: the site's database password stays readable by the bench user only                                                                                                                               | —                                                 |
| Processes                                    | The bench user's systemd **user** units, `<bench>-<process>.service`, as `wolf-pilot-export` copies them (`bench_processes_down`). The Admin is socket-activated: inactive until its first request is not down | checked                                           |
| Deployments                                  | A `deployment` event (category `pilot`) when a task such as update, migrate or app install **starts**, and an `error` event (`pilot_task_failed`) when one fails, from `wolf-pilot-export`'s copy              | checked with a migrate run from the Admin         |
| "Enable Wolf for this bench" toggle in Pilot | Needs a change in frappe/pilot                                                                                                                                                                                 | **not done**                                      |

The metrics themselves are described on [What is collected](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/collected).

## Bench layout

### Benches

Pilot's `install.sh` installs into `$HOME/pilot` as a non-root bench user (`frappe` by default). Benches live in `~/pilot/benches/<name>/`, each with `apps/`, `sites/`, `env/`, `logs/`, `config/`, `tasks/` and `bench.toml`.

### bench.toml

Mode `0600`, readable by the bench user only. Wolf reads it at registration, which runs as root:

| Key                    | Use                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `[bench] name`         | Required, together with `python`. The bench name and the Pilot marker                                                |
| `[redis] queue_port`   | Queue Redis port. Default `11000`                                                                                    |
| `[admin] port`         | Default `7000`. The Admin backend listens on `127.0.0.1:<port + 1>`                                                  |
| `[admin] jwt_secret`   | Only when Wolf mints an Admin token, which needs `bench.toml` readable. Pilot writes it at the Admin's first session |
| `[production] enabled` | Kept for information                                                                                                 |

### Processes and logs

Pilot runs a production bench as **systemd user units** of the bench user (`systemctl --user`), with linger on: `<bench>-web`, `<bench>-redis_cache`, `<bench>-redis_queue`, `<bench>-admin` (socket-activated, `<bench>-admin.socket`) and app processes. Pilot's MariaDB is the user unit `pilot-mariadb`.

**Lite mode**, on by default (`[lite_mode] enabled`), runs the web server, the job workers and the scheduler in one `web` process (`frappe.runner`). Its logs, Python's `logging` output included, go to `logs/web.log.error.log`. Out of lite mode there are worker and schedule processes, logged as `worker_<queue-slug>_<i>.log` and `schedule.log`, with stderr in `<log>.error.log`.

**The sandbox.** A new systemd bench runs its workload sandboxed, and Frappe's own logs (`frappe.log`, `scheduler.log`…) are then in `logs/workload/`. The sandbox needs unprivileged user namespaces, which Ubuntu 24.04 refuses by default (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1`): `pilot setup production` then fails, and Pilot advises `sandbox = false` under `[production]`. Wolf reads both layouts.

### nginx

Each site vhost logs to `<bench>/logs/nginx-access.log`:

```nginx
log_format pilot_access '$pilot_client_addr [$time_local] "$request_method $uri" $status "$host" $request_time';
```

This format has **no query string** (`$uri`, not `$request_uri`) and **no User-Agent**. On a Pilot bench, Wolf's [web detection](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/detection) sees probed paths (`/.env`, `/.git/`, CMS and appliance paths) but not injections or path traversal carried in a query string, nor scanners named by their User-Agent. [Suricata](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/wazuh-suricata#suricata) sees the full requests.

### Tasks

Admin operations are tasks, stored as `<bench>/tasks/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-hex>/`, mode `0700`:

- `meta.json`: `task_id`, `command`, `args`, `queued_at`, `started_at`, `finished_at` (UTC ISO-8601), `exit_code`, `failure`.
- `status`: `queued`, `running`, `success`, `failed` or `killed`.

## Deployment events from Pilot tasks

Wolf reports these task commands:

`update`, `retry-update`, `complete-migration`, `migrate`, `revert-migration`, `revert-apps`, `revert-site`, `switch-branch`, `get-and-install-app`, `install-app`, `uninstall-app`, `remove-app`, `build`, `restart-services`, `switch-lite-mode`, `setup-nginx`, `restore-site`, `reinstall-site`.

The site comes from the task's `site` / `sites` arguments; nothing else of the arguments is kept.

### Where tasks are read

1. **Task files**, `<bench>/tasks/*/meta.json` and `status`, when the agent can read them (an agent run as the bench user).
2. **`wolf-pilot-export`'s copy**, `/var/lib/wolf-pilot-export/<bench>.json`, when it is less than 5 minutes old: the normal case.
3. **Admin API**, `GET http://127.0.0.1:<admin.port+1>/api/v1/tasks?limit=100`, only without the two others. It needs a bench-scoped token: `pilot.token`, or one Wolf mints from `pilot.jwt_secret` or `bench.toml`. Pilot lists every token it verifies among the Admin's active sessions, and a bench-scoped token can do everything the Admin can: the copy avoids both.

### How events are produced

The same rules as on [Press servers](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/press):

- A `deployment` event is sent when the task starts, timestamped at `started_at`. An incident during a long migrate links to it, for example through the "502 spike after deployment" [preset](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/presets).
- An `error` event is sent if the task ends `failed`. It carries `failure.code`, `failure.message` and `exit_code`.
- Reported task ids are kept for 3 days in `<spool_dir>/pilot-tasks.json`.
- The first poll skips history and only picks up queued or running tasks.

A migrate also records the site's own `deployment` event (source `frappe`), as on any bench: Pilot's says which task ran it.

## Wolf next to Pilot's own monitoring

From the Pilot docs:

- `pilot-monitor.service` collects host, database and bench metrics and pings production sites.
- `[resource_limits]` raises CPU, memory, disk and uptime alerts after 5 minutes. They go to Central (on Central-managed hosts), to `webhook_endpoints` and to mail.
- `[telemetry]` ships metrics and logs to a region's "Datum" endpoint with a Central-issued token.

Wolf reads the same local files and does not interfere with any of these. What it adds on a self-hosted Pilot host:

- Tracebacks, failed scheduled jobs and worker crashes as events.
- 5xx/502 per site.
- SSH signals.
- Incidents tied to the Pilot task that preceded them.

All of it is kept on your own Wolf site.

## The Wolf App on a Pilot bench

The Wolf App installs on a Pilot bench like any app (`pilot get-app`, `pilot install-app`). Pilot checks that every app an app requires in `hooks.py` is declared in its `pyproject.toml` `[tool.bench.frappe-dependencies]`, Frappe excepted: Frappe is implicit, and an app that lists it in `required_apps` is refused.

## What Pilot would need

1. **"Enable Wolf for this bench" toggle.** A `[wolf]` table in `bench.toml` (`enabled`, `url`) plus an Admin settings switch, which would install and register the agent. It belongs in frappe/pilot.
2. **A read-only machine token for the Admin API** (`tasks:read`, unit states), which would make the root helper unnecessary.
3. **The query string and User-Agent in `pilot_access`**, for web attack detection from the access log.


# What is collected

Run `wolf-agent check` to see the exact payload on your host. Each check below can be turned off or
tuned in the [configuration](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/configuration).

## Host

From `/proc`, every push (`push_interval`, 30 s):

| Metric                                            | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `cpu_usage`                                       | percent                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `memory_used_percent`, `swap_used_percent`        |                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `load_1m`, `load_5m`, `load_15m`, `load_per_core` |                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `disk_used_percent`                               | per real mount, label `mount`                                                                                                                                                        |
| `agent_setup_failed`, `agent_setup_warnings`      | every hour: the failures and warnings of the agent's own [`wolf-agent doctor`](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/commands#check-a-host) run, listed on the Monitoring page |

## Bench logs

From `<bench>/logs/`, and the site-scoped `sites/<site>/logs/frappe.web.log` and `scheduler.log`:

| Log                                            | Becomes                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `frappe.web.log`, `web.error.log`, `bench.log` | `error` events with the traceback                               |
| `scheduler.log`                                | `cron_failure` events for failed scheduled jobs                 |
| `worker.log`, `worker.error.log`               | `worker_failure` events: worker crashes, OOM kills, failed jobs |

::note
Frappe logs "Scheduled Job Failed" at INFO, which the default logger drops. To catch every failing
cron, also install the app on each site as a [satellite](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/every-site).
::

## nginx access log

Per site and per minute of the log line's own time: `http_requests`, `http_5xx`, `http_502`, plus
one aggregated event per (site, status, route) and minute. Each sample is stamped with the newest
line of its minute, so a backlog read at once (after a restart or a rotation) lands in the minutes
it happened, not as one spike when the agent reads it. A known site with no traffic reports zeros.

The site comes from `$host` when the log format includes it (a leading vhost field or a trailing
quoted field), else from a per-site log file name, else the bench's only site.

The same lines feed [web attack detection](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/detection): probes for secrets, admin panels,
traversal and injections become `web_attack_probe` events, and a secret-bearing file answered with
a 2xx becomes a critical `web_sensitive_file_exposed` event.

## Auth log

From `/var/log/auth.log`, `/var/log/secure`, or `journalctl` (`sshd`, `sshd-session`, `sudo`,
`useradd`, `usermod`, `gpasswd`, `chsh`):

| Signal                                                                          | Event                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| failed SSH logins, aggregated per source IP and minute of log time; root logins | `security`                                                                                                    |
| a successful login from an address that failed 5+ times in the hour before      | `ssh_login_after_failures` (critical)                                                                         |
| failed sudo attempts, users outside sudoers                                     | `sudo_failure`                                                                                                |
| new local accounts                                                              | `account_created`; a package's service account (system UID, no login shell): `service_account_created` (info) |
| a user added to `sudo`, `wheel`, `admin`, `root`, `adm`, `docker` or `lxd`      | `admin_group_change` (critical)                                                                               |

## Redis and RQ

From the bench's queue Redis (`redis_queue`):

| Metric                                            | Meaning                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `queue_length`                                    | length of every `rq:queue:*` list                   |
| `rq_failed_jobs`, `rq_failed_jobs_added`          | failed-job registry size, and its increase per push |
| `rq_long_running_jobs`                            | started jobs older than `rq.long_job_minutes` (30)  |
| `rq_workers`                                      | live workers                                        |
| `redis_used_memory_percent`, `redis_evicted_keys` | from `INFO`                                         |

Only the queue Redis is watched. The cache Redis is an LRU cache by design (`allkeys-lru`), so a
full cache and evictions are normal there.

## Backups

`backup_age_hours` per site, from the newest `sites/<site>/private/backups/*-database.sql*`, every
10 minutes. A site that never had a backup sends nothing, so *No backup for 26 h* cannot fire for it.
On Press benches it comes from the Press agent's newest successful **Backup Site** job instead
(Press deletes offsite backups from the server), and a failed one sends a `backup_failed` event.
Other offsite-only setups can point `backups.dirs` at a mounted directory per site.

## TLS certificates

`tls_days_left` for every public site name and custom domain (`site_config.json` `domains`), every
hour, in a background thread. The agent connects to `<domain>:443` with SNI and reads the leaf
certificate without verifying it, so expired and self-signed certificates are measured too.

Skipped: `localhost`, `*.localhost`, `.local`, `.test`, bare names, IP addresses and the `example.*`
names. Unreachable domains are logged and skipped.

## MariaDB

Through the `mariadb` (or `mysql`) client, with a site's own credentials written to a private
temporary option file, never on the command line:

| Metric                                                 | Meaning                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| `db_threads_connected`, `db_connections_used_percent`  | against `max_connections` |
| `db_slow_queries`                                      | increase per push         |
| `db_replication_lag_seconds`, `db_replication_running` | on a replica              |

A site user may not read replica status (REPLICATION CLIENT / SLAVE MONITOR). Then replication is
skipped, unless `mariadb.user` / `password` or `mariadb.defaults_file` names a monitoring user.
Without a client on the host, or for Postgres benches, nothing is sent.

## Processes

From `supervisorctl status`, else `systemctl list-units` for units whose name contains the bench name.
`bench_processes_down` per bench counts processes that are STOPPED, EXITED, BACKOFF, FATAL or
UNKNOWN (systemd: `failed` or a restart loop). A process entering FATAL / UNKNOWN (systemd `failed`)
also sends one `worker_failure` / `process_down` event. Press benches run processes in containers
and are skipped.

## Security posture

| Check                    | Every  | Sends                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------ | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **App versions**         | 1 h    | `app_version` per bench and app, from `apps/<app>/<app>/__init__.py`. The Wolf site compares them with the GitHub Security Advisories of Frappe and ERPNext. Development versions are not sent.                                                                                                                                         |
| **Site settings**        | 1 h    | `site_setting` per site: two-factor authentication, password policy and minimum score, lockout, guest uploads, and the System Manager role's two-factor flag. Feeds the [security score](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/compliance) of sites other than the Wolf site.                                                  |
| **Exposure**             | 10 min | `exposed_services` per host: bench ports listening beyond loopback (MariaDB 3306, Postgres 5432, Redis, socket.io 9000, gunicorn). `site_config_risks` per site: `developer_mode`, `allow_tests`, a plain-HTTP `host_name`, `allow_cors: "*"`.                                                                                          |
| **File integrity**       | 15 min | `integrity_files` per bench; `bench_code_changed` and `bench_config_changed` events when an app's code, a site config or the nginx and supervisor config changes, telling a deployment from a change outside one. See [Detection](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/detection#file-integrity).                             |
| **Outbound connections** | 1 min  | `bench_outbound_destinations` per bench; a `bench_new_outbound` event for each public network and unusual port a bench's user had never used, after a 7-day learning period; `bench_new_outbound_usual` counts new ones on usual ports. See [Detection](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/detection#outbound-connections). |

See [Detection](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/detection).

## Optional sources

When present on the host, the agent also tails:

- **Suricata**'s EVE log, found from Suricata itself ([how](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/wazuh-suricata#turn-it-on)): `network_ids_alert` events;
- **Wazuh**'s `alerts.json` on the manager: `hids_alert` events.

See [Wazuh and Suricata](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/wazuh-suricata).

## Delivery guarantees

- Logs are read from the end on first start. Offsets are kept in
  `/var/lib/wolf-agent/spool/tail-state.json`, so restarts and log rotation lose nothing.
- Failed pushes are spooled to `/var/lib/wolf-agent/spool/outbox/` (capped at 50 MB) and replayed in
  order with exponential backoff.
- Events are [scrubbed](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/scrubbing) of e-mail addresses, credentials, card numbers and IBANs
  before they are spooled.


# Configuration

`wolf-agent register` writes `/etc/wolf-agent/config.json` (mode 0600, owned by `wolf-agent`).
Edit it to add logs or override discovery, then restart the service:

```bash [host]
sudo systemctl restart wolf-agent
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent check   # runs every check once, TLS included
```

Use another file with `--config PATH` or `$WOLF_AGENT_CONFIG`.

## Full example

```json [/etc/wolf-agent/config.json]
{
  "url": "https://wolf.example.com",
  "agent_id": "WAG-0001",
  "agent_secret": "…",
  "hostname": "bench-01",
  "push_interval": 30,
  "spool_dir": "/var/lib/wolf-agent/spool",
  "verify_tls": true,
  "auth_log": null,
  "collect_host_metrics": true,
  "platform": null,
  "press": {"agent_dir": "/home/frappe/agent", "benches_directory": null, "nginx_access_log": "/var/log/nginx/access.log",
            "rediscover_interval": 60, "deployments": true},
  "pilot": {"deployments": true, "api_url": null, "token": null, "jwt_secret": null},
  "benches": [
    {"name": "frappe-bench", "path": "/home/frappe/frappe-bench", "sites": ["a.example.com"],
     "logs_dir": "/home/frappe/frappe-bench/logs", "nginx_access_log": "/var/log/nginx/access.log",
     "redis_queue": "redis://127.0.0.1:11000"}
  ],
  "extra_logs": [{"path": "/var/log/myapp/error.log", "parser": "traceback", "bench": null, "site": null}],
  "rq": {"long_job_minutes": 30},
  "backups": {"enabled": true, "interval": 600, "press": false, "dirs": {}},
  "tls": {"enabled": true, "interval": 3600, "port": 443, "timeout": 5, "connect_host": null,
```
