```json [/etc/wolf-agent/config.json]
          "domains": ["status.example.com"], "exclude": []},
  "mariadb": {"enabled": true, "cli": null, "host": null, "port": null, "user": null,
              "password": null, "defaults_file": null},
  "processes": {"enabled": true, "manager": "auto"},
  "versions": {"enabled": true, "interval": 3600},
  "site_settings": {"enabled": true, "interval": 3600},
  "suricata": {"enabled": true, "eve_log": null, "max_priority": 3, "exclude_sids": [2012888]},
  "wazuh": {"enabled": true, "alerts_log": null, "min_level": 7, "exclude_groups": ["sca"]},
  "scrub": {"enabled": true, "ips": false, "extra_patterns": [], "keep": []},
  "watchdog": {
    "enabled": true,
    "stale_minutes": 5,
    "webhook_url": "https://chat.example.com/hooks/xxxx",
    "smtp": {"host": "smtp.example.com", "port": 587, "starttls": true, "from": "wolf@example.com",
             "to": ["ops@example.com"], "user": "wolf", "password": "…"}
  }
}
```

## Connection

::field-group
  :::field{name="url" type="string"}
  The central Wolf site.
  :::

  :::field{name="agent_id / agent_secret" type="string"}
  Written by `register`. The site keeps only a hash of the secret: to replace a lost one, use
  **Rotate secret** on the Wolf Agent form.
  :::

  :::field{name="push_interval" type="number"}
  Seconds between pushes. Default `30`.
  :::

  :::field{name="verify_tls" type="boolean"}
  Verify the Wolf site's certificate. Default `true`.
  :::

  :::field{name="spool_dir" type="string"}
  Tail offsets, the outbox of failed pushes (50 MB cap) and the watchdog state.
  :::
::

## Sources

::field-group
  :::field{name="platform" type="null | "press" | "generic""}
  `null` auto-detects [Press](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/press), `"press"` forces it, `"generic"` disables it.
  :::

  :::field{name="benches" type="array"}
  Name, path, sites, `logs_dir`, `nginx_access_log` (a path or a list) and `redis_queue` per bench.
  Filled by discovery; edit to override.
  :::

  :::field{name="auth_log" type="null | string | "journal" | false"}
  `null` auto-detects, a path forces a file, `"journal"` forces journalctl, `false` disables.
  :::

  :::field{name="collect_host_metrics" type="boolean"}
  CPU, memory, swap, load and disk. Default `true`.
  :::

  :::field{name="extra_logs" type="array"}
  More files to tail: `path`, `parser` (`traceback`, `scheduler`, `worker`, `nginx`, `auth`), and
  optional `bench` and `site`.
  :::

  :::field{name="pilot" type="object"}
  `deployments`, `api_url`, `token`, `jwt_secret`. See [Pilot benches](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/pilot).
  :::

  :::field{name="press" type="object"}
  `agent_dir`, `benches_directory`, `nginx_access_log`, `rediscover_interval` (s), `deployments`. See
  [Press servers](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/press).
  :::
::

## Checks

Every key is optional; the defaults are those of the example. `"tls": false` (and the same for the
others) turns a check off.

| Key             | Settings                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rq`            | `long_job_minutes` (30)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `backups`       | `enabled`, `interval` (600 s), `press` (skip Press benches), `dirs` (backup directory per site)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `tls`           | `interval` (3600 s), `port` (443), `timeout` (5 s), `connect_host` (for example `127.0.0.1` to check the local nginx), `domains` (add), `exclude` (drop)                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `mariadb`       | `cli` (else `mariadb` / `mysql`), `host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `defaults_file`: a monitoring user for replication status                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `processes`     | `manager`: `auto`, `supervisor` or `systemd`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `versions`      | `interval` (3600 s)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `site_settings` | `interval` (3600 s)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `exposure`      | `interval` (600 s), `ports` (more ports to count)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `integrity`     | `interval` (900 s), `full_scan_interval` (86400 s), `server_paths` (`null`: `/etc/nginx` and `/etc/supervisor`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `outbound`      | `interval` (60 s), `learn_days` (7), `include_private` (`false`), `usual_ports` (ports only counted, added to the defaults), `report_usual_ports` (`false`), `proxy_logs` (`null`: `/var/log/squid/access.log` when it exists; or `[{"path", "format": "squid"}]`), `kernel_log` (`"auto"`: every new connection when `wolf-outbound-log` is installed; `false`) |
| `suricata`      | `eve_log`, `max_priority` (3), `exclude_sids` (`[2012888]`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `setup_checks`  | `enabled`, `interval` (3600 s): the agent's own `wolf-agent doctor` run, sent to the Monitoring page                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `wazuh`         | `alerts_log`, `min_level` (7), `exclude_groups` (`["sca"]`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

## Privacy and safety

| Key        | Page                                                                             |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scrub`    | [Scrubbing](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/scrubbing)               |
| `watchdog` | [Watchdog](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/watchdog)                 |
| `response` | [Response actions](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/response-actions) |


# Commands

Run commands as the `wolf-agent` user, which owns the config:
`sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent <command>`.

Global options: `--config PATH` (or `$WOLF_AGENT_CONFIG`), `-v`.

| Command                                                                                   | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `register --url URL --token TOKEN [--bench PATH]...`                                      | Register the host, discover benches, write the config.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `run`                                                                                     | The daemon loop. This is what systemd runs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `refresh`                                                                                 | As root: read again what the agent's user cannot (a Press server's benches folder and proxy; a Press proxy's access log) and save it in the config, without registering again. `install.sh` runs it on every upgrade.                                                                                                                            |
| `discover [--bench PATH] [--platform auto|press|generic]`                                 | Show what bench discovery finds.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `check [--from-start] [--status] [--platform …]`                                          | Collect once and print the JSON payload. Nothing is sent. The watchdog state goes to stderr. `--status` also asks the site for its health.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `doctor [--json] [--offline]`                                                             | Check what this host gives the agent and what to fix: registration and the Wolf site, each log, bench, queue Redis and nginx log, the Press job database or Pilot export, the auth log or journal, response actions, the daemon. Read-only. Exits 1 when a check fails. See [Check a host](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#check-a-host). |
| `mark-deployment --bench NAME [--site S] [--note TEXT] [--silence 15m]`                   | Put a deployment marker on the Wolf timeline. `--silence` also opens a maintenance window that mutes notifications for that bench or site.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `test-fallback`                                                                           | Send a test message through the [watchdog](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/watchdog) fallback channels.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `demo press|multi|single [--root DIR] [--days N] [--no-live] [--cycle MIN] [--configure]` | Write a simulated server for this agent to read: days of history, then live traffic and incidents. For demos and tests only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Mark a deployment

```bash [deploy.sh]
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent mark-deployment --bench frappe-bench --site erp.example.com \
  --note "ERPNext v15.42 + custom app 2.3" --silence 15m
```

The marker is a `deployment` event. Rules with **Require recent deployment** only fire after one,
and incidents link to the latest deployment of their scope. Text passed with `--note` is sent as is,
without [scrubbing](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/scrubbing).

Press and Pilot tasks, and `bench migrate` on sites running the Wolf App, are marked by themselves.

## Run a demo

`demo KIND` lays out a simulated server under `--root` (default `/home/frappe/demo-KIND`). Sites are
names only: nothing runs behind them.

| Kind     | Server                                                                                                                       | Deployments                                                       |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `press`  | a Press app server: 3 benches, 8 sites (two with a custom domain), the Press agent's `jobs.sqlite3`, nginx in Press's format | Press jobs, read by the agent                                     |
| `multi`  | plain benches: 2 benches, 6 sites (two with a custom domain), one nginx log with `$host` first                               | marked through the deployment endpoint, as `mark-deployment` does |
| `single` | one bench, one site                                                                                                          | same as `multi`                                                   |

Every kind has an auth.log too. Use a host or container of its own, registered under a name of its own:

```bash [demo host]
wolf-agent register --url https://wolf.example.com --token TOKEN --hostname dokos-multi-1 --bench /home/frappe/demo-multi
wolf-agent demo multi --configure   # points the agent at the demo; checks with nothing behind them off
wolf-agent run &                    # the agent runs first: it must open the files while they are empty
wolf-agent demo multi               # 7 days of history, then an incident cycle every 30 minutes
```

`--bench` names a directory that is not a bench yet, so the host registers without benches; the
demo's benches reach Wolf with its telemetry. For `press`, also pass `--platform press`.

The demo waits until the agent tracks every file, then writes the history, which reaches Wolf
through the agent's own discovery, tailers and parsers. Past host metrics, which the agent samples
live, go through its spool. Each cycle has a deployment followed by 4 minutes of 502s, a request
traceback, a failed scheduled job, a killed worker, an SSH brute force (every third one succeeds),
a web attack scan and, every other cycle, a failed bench operation (a Press Patch App job, or a
`bench update` traceback).

Rules look at the last minutes, so incidents open for the live cycles, not for the history.
`bench --site SITE generate-demo-press` (or `-multi`, `-single`) with `--agent-config PATH` does the
same from a bench that has the agent installed, and `--webhook URL` also sends the demo's alerts
there. The [development page](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/development) runs it all in Docker.

## Check a host

```bash [host]
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent doctor
```

Run it as the agent's user: root can read what the daemon cannot, and would hide problems. Each line is **ok**, **WARN**, **FAIL** or `--` (for information), with the fix after a warning or a failure:

```text
logs
  ok   18 log file(s) readable
  --   9 not written yet (read once they appear): bench-1/frappe.web.log ...

platform
 FAIL  Press: /home/frappe/agent/jobs.sqlite3-wal is not the Press agent's: its jobs fail to write
        fix: stop the Press agent (supervisorctl stop 'agent:'), delete ...-wal and -shm, start it
```

It checks the files the daemon would tail and the benches it works from (on Press, the ones it rediscovers), not only the config. `--json` prints the checks as a list, `--offline` skips the call to the Wolf site. Nothing is written, and it exits 1 when a check fails, so it can gate an install script.

The daemon runs the same checks every hour (`setup_checks`) and sends them with a push: the Wolf UI's **Monitoring** page shows each host's setup, its problems and their fixes, and the *Host setup problem* preset opens an incident while a check fails.

## See the payload

```bash [host]
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent check --from-start | jq '.events[] | {type, category, title}'
```

`--from-start` reads the logs from the beginning instead of the saved offsets, which is useful to
test a parser on an existing file. `check` never sends anything and never moves the offsets.


# Scrubbing

Before an event is spooled or sent, the agent scrubs its title and every string in its payload:
sample lines, tracebacks, messages, routes. It is on by default.

| What                                                                                                                                                                       | Becomes                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| e-mail addresses, also URL-encoded (`jane%40example.com`)                                                                                                                  | `[EMAIL]`                                      |
| `Authorization:` / `Proxy-Authorization:` header values, `Cookie:` / `Set-Cookie:` values                                                                                  | `[REDACTED]`                                   |
| `Bearer …`, `token <key>:<secret>`, `Basic …` credentials                                                                                                                  | `[REDACTED]`                                   |
| JWTs (`eyJ….….…`)                                                                                                                                                          | `[JWT]`                                        |
| values of `password`, `pwd`, `new_password`, `*_secret`, `*_token`, `api_key`, `sid`, `session_id`, `otp`, `signature`, in query strings, forms, JSON or Python dict reprs | `[REDACTED]`                                   |
| card-like numbers (13–19 digits, Luhn-valid, issuer digit 2–6)                                                                                                             | `[CARD]`                                       |
| IBAN-like strings (mod-97 checked)                                                                                                                                         | `[IBAN]`                                       |
| IP addresses, only with `"ips": true`                                                                                                                                      | `[IP:<8 hex>]`, a keyed hash, stable per agent |

## IP addresses

IPs are kept by default, because the SSH brute-force and "admin login from a new IP" rules are built
on them. Turn `ips` on if addresses count as personal data for you and you can live without per-IP
grouping in titles.

## What never changes

Type, host, bench, site, timestamp and fingerprint. Fingerprints are computed from the raw lines
before scrubbing, so grouping and deduplication on the Wolf site work the same either way.

Metrics carry no free text and are not scrubbed. Text you type yourself
(`mark-deployment --note`) is sent as is.

## Settings

```json [/etc/wolf-agent/config.json]
"scrub": {
  "enabled": true,
  "ips": false,
  "extra_patterns": [
    "internal-\\d{4}",
    {"pattern": "CUST-\\d{6}", "replacement": "[CUSTOMER]"}
  ],
  "keep": ["@dokos.io", "noreply@example.com"]
}
```

::field-group
  :::field{name="extra_patterns" type="array"}
  More regexes: a string (replaced by `[REDACTED]`) or `{"pattern", "replacement"}`. Invalid ones
  are logged and skipped.
  :::

  :::field{name="keep" type="array"}
  Values never replaced: exact strings (case-insensitive), or `@domain` to keep every address at that
  domain, such as your own system mails.
  :::

  :::field{name="enabled" type="boolean"}
  `"scrub": false` or `"enabled": false` ships the lines as they are.
  :::
::

Run `wolf-agent check` to see exactly what would be sent.


# Watchdog

Wolf alerts are sent by the Wolf site. When that site, its database or its scheduler is down,
nobody would hear about it. So the agent watches the site and alerts through its own **fallback
channel**, which does not go through the site.

## When it alerts

Every push response carries the site's `health` ([protocol](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/protocol)). The agent raises
an outage when:

- pushes have failed for `stale_minutes`: the site, a proxy or the database is down;
- the site reports its alert rules (or, with no rule enabled, its scheduled jobs) have not run for
  `stale_minutes`: scheduler stopped or paused, no worker, Redis down, or stored times pushed into
  the future by a time-zone change;
- queued pushes have waited `stale_minutes` for a worker. In `async` ingest mode, the site answers
  before storing, so pushes look fine while nothing is stored.

It sends one alert per outage, then one recovery notice when pushes work and rules run again. The
state is kept in `<spool_dir>/watchdog-state.json`, so a restart neither repeats the alert nor
forgets the outage. A failed delivery is retried every minute.

If the site rejects the agent's credentials, a last alert goes out before the agent exits.

## Channels

Both are optional. When both are set, both are used.

```json [/etc/wolf-agent/config.json]
"watchdog": {
  "enabled": true,
  "stale_minutes": 5,
  "webhook_url": "https://chat.example.com/hooks/xxxx",
  "smtp": {"host": "smtp.example.com", "port": 587, "starttls": true,
           "from": "wolf@example.com", "to": ["ops@example.com"],
           "user": "wolf", "password": "…"}
}
```

::field-group
  :::field{name="webhook_url" type="string"}
  POSTs `{"text": "..."}`, which Slack, Mattermost and Rocket.Chat incoming webhooks accept.
  :::

  :::field{name="smtp" type="object"}
  `host`, `port` (default 25; 587 with `starttls`, 465 with `ssl`), `from`, `to` (list or
  comma-separated), `starttls` (default on for port 587), `ssl`, `user`, `password`, `verify_tls`.
  :::

  :::field{name="stale_minutes" type="number"}
  Default `5`.
  :::
::

With no channel, the watchdog only logs to the journal at ERROR level. `"enabled": false` turns it
off.

```bash [host]
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent test-fallback   # after editing the config
sudo -u wolf-agent wolf-agent check           # shows the watchdog state on stderr
```

::tip
Point the fallback at a channel that does not depend on the Wolf site's host: another mail relay,
or a chat webhook.
::

## On the timeline afterwards

While its rules are stale, the site records a `scheduler_stalled` event on each push. The
**Scheduler stalled** preset turns it into an incident once the scheduler runs again, so the outage
appears on the Wolf timeline.


# Response actions

Wolf proposes, a Wolf Manager approves each action with a second click, and nothing runs on its
own. Every approval is a **Wolf Response Action** row (who, when, what, result; read-only for
everyone) and a comment on the incident.

| Action                                                          | Proposed for                                                                                                           | Applied by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Block IP for N hours** (1 to 168, default 24)                 | the public addresses of the incident's security events, from any source (Wolf, Suricata, Wazuh), for the attacked host | the Wolf Agent on that host, with its next push, when allowed there (below), and/or [Wazuh active response](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#wazuh-active-response); and [CrowdSec](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#crowdsec) when set up |
| **Disable user**, **log out all sessions**, **revoke API keys** | the users named by the site's own security events (failed logins, new IP or country, role granted, API key generated)  | the Wolf site, at once                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

- Approve from the incident's **Response** panel in the Wolf UI, or from the signed link in the
  alert (up to 5 per alert). The link only shows the proposal: a guest is sent to the login page,
  only a logged-in Wolf Manager or System Manager gets the button, and only its POST acts. A
  forwarded email alone cannot act, and a link opened again says the action was done.
- Only what Wolf proposed from the incident's own events can be approved: the API refuses any
  other action, target or host.
- Administrator, Guest and the approver's own account are refused. Only a System Manager can act
  on a System Manager. User actions apply to the Wolf site only.
- Blocks are marked *Expired* once their time is over (hourly).

## Blocking on the host

The agent does nothing unless you allow it on that host.

::note
**Behind a proxy.** A block on a host only stops what reaches it directly. On a Press app server behind its proxy, a web client's packets come from the proxy, so Wolf proposes blocks there for SSH events only. The Response panel lists the other addresses as *Not proposed*, naming the proxy. The Wolf Agent on the [proxy server](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/press#proxy-servers) proposes their blocks, where they take effect.
::

::caution
The agent refuses private, loopback and reserved addresses, and durations over a week, whatever
the site sends. It runs the command as a list of arguments, never through a shell. Without
`response.enabled`, each action comes back *Failed* with the reason, so the manager knows it was
not applied.
::

### Set up

::note
An agent installed before this fix has `NoNewPrivileges=yes` in `/etc/systemd/system/wolf-agent.service`, which stops `sudo`: no block ever ran. Re-run `install.sh`, or delete that line, then `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart wolf-agent`.

`install.sh` does not install the helpers below: after an upgrade, copy `wolf-block` (or `wolf-block-fail2ban`) again with the `install` line of its tab. Older copies let a shorter block of an address cut short a longer one.
::

::tabs
  :::tabs-item{label="nftables"}
  ```bash [host]
  install -m 0755 -o root -g root agent/wolf-block.sh /usr/local/sbin/wolf-block
  echo 'wolf-agent ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/local/sbin/wolf-block' > /etc/sudoers.d/wolf-block
  chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/wolf-block
  ```

  In the agent config:

  ```json [/etc/wolf-agent/config.json]
  "response": {"enabled": true}
  ```

  Restart the agent. `wolf-block` adds the address to an nftables set (`inet wolf`, `blocked4` /
  `blocked6`) whose entries expire by themselves. `nft list table inet wolf` shows them. Blocking
  an address that is already blocked keeps the longer of the two blocks.
  :::

  :::tabs-item{label="fail2ban"}
  Where fail2ban already manages the firewall, `wolf-block-fail2ban` bans in a jail of its own
  (`wolf`), with your usual ban action:

  ```bash [host]
  cp agent/fail2ban/wolf.local /etc/fail2ban/jail.d/wolf.local && fail2ban-client reload
  install -m 0755 -o root -g root agent/wolf-block-fail2ban.sh /usr/local/sbin/wolf-block-fail2ban
  install -d -m 0700 /var/lib/wolf-block   # the expiries; writable from the agent's unit
  echo 'wolf-agent ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/local/sbin/wolf-block-fail2ban' > /etc/sudoers.d/wolf-block
  chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/wolf-block
  # reboots lose the scheduled unbans: sweep the expired ones every 5 minutes
  echo '*/5 * * * * root /usr/local/sbin/wolf-block-fail2ban --sweep >/dev/null' > /etc/cron.d/wolf-block-fail2ban
  ```

  In the agent config:

  ```json [/etc/wolf-agent/config.json]
  "response": {"enabled": true, "command": ["sudo", "-n", "/usr/local/sbin/wolf-block-fail2ban", "{ip}", "{seconds}"]}
  ```

  `fail2ban-client get wolf banip` lists the addresses. `fail2ban-client set wolf unbanip IP` lifts
  one early. Without the jail, the helper refuses and says so, and the action comes back *Failed*.
  :::
::

Paths are relative to a checkout of the repository.

### Custom command

`response.command` replaces the command. `{ip}` and `{seconds}` are filled in.

### How fail2ban durations work

fail2ban has no per-ban duration: every ban gets the jail's `bantime`. The jail's is the longest
block Wolf asks for (7 days), and the helper unbans each address when its own duration is over:

- each expiry is written to `/var/lib/wolf-block/fail2ban.state`, and `--sweep` unbans those that
  are over. Banning an address again keeps the later expiry;
- a transient systemd timer (`wolf-unban-<ip>-<time>`) runs `--sweep` at the expiry, so an earlier
  timer leaves a longer ban alone.

Timers do not survive a reboot, and fail2ban restores its bans after one. Without the cron line, a
block could last up to the jail's 7 days. The helper also sweeps on each ban.

## Wazuh active response

With **Block With** set to `wazuh` or `both` (**Wolf Settings → Blocking**), an approved block runs
through Wazuh active response on the Wazuh agent of the attacked host, through the Wazuh manager's
API. It is the same approval, the same signed links, the same journal: only who applies the block
changes.

| Block With             | Who applies an approved block                                     |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `wolf_agent` (default) | the Wolf Agent on the attacked host, as above                     |
| `wazuh`                | Wazuh active response on that host's Wazuh agent                  |
| `both`                 | each of them: two **Wolf Response Action** rows, one per executor |

A block is proposed for the host that was attacked, not for the agent that sent the alert: a Wazuh
or Suricata alert, read on the manager's or the sensor's host, or posted by the integration, is
about the host it names. Any other agent's event is about that agent's own host, whatever its
`host` says, so an agent cannot point a block at another machine. With
`wolf_agent`, a host without a Wolf Agent gets no block proposal; with `wazuh` or `both`, it does.

::steps{level="3"}
### Define a timed command on the Wazuh manager

Wolf runs a *named* command, which Wazuh removes by itself when its timeout runs out. Add an
`<active-response>` block for `firewall-drop` with the timeout you want, on a rule that never fires
so that it only runs when Wolf asks, then restart the manager:

```xml [ossec.conf]
<active-response>
  <disabled>no</disabled>
  <command>firewall-drop</command>
  <location>local</location>
  <rules_id>999999</rules_id>
  <timeout>86400</timeout>
</active-response>
```

Wazuh names the command with its timeout: `firewall-drop86400` (listed in
`/var/ossec/etc/shared/ar.conf`). That timeout is the block's duration; the hours chosen at approval
only apply to the Wolf Agent's block. A script (`!firewall-drop`) is refused: Wazuh never removes it.

### Create a Wazuh API user

A user allowed to read agents and run active response commands (`agent:read`,
`active-response:command`).

### Fill Wolf Settings → Blocking

| Field                                      | Value                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Block With**                             | `wazuh` or `both`                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Wazuh Active Response Command**          | `firewall-drop86400`                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Wazuh API URL**                          | `https://wazuh-manager:55000`. `http://` only to the same machine (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`): the password goes with every login. Changing the URL asks for the password again. |
| **Wazuh API User**, **Wazuh API Password** | the user above                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Verify Wazuh TLS Certificate**           | on, unless the manager has a self-signed certificate on a trusted network                                                                                                       |
::

- Wolf finds the Wazuh agent by the host's names (its Wolf hostname, its
  [aliases](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/wazuh-suricata#aliases)), then by an address only one Wazuh agent has: hosts
  behind one NAT share theirs. The manager (`000`) never runs a block. When no agent matches, the action is *Failed* with the reason; add a Wolf Entity
  Alias and approve again.
- The action is *Applied* or *Failed* at once, with Wazuh's answer, and journaled like any other.
  It is recorded before Wolf calls Wazuh, so a block Wazuh applied always has its row.
- With `both`, each executor has its own duration (the hours asked for the Wolf Agent, the
  command's timeout for Wazuh) and its own row. When Wazuh's half fails, it alone is proposed
  again while the Wolf Agent's half waits for its agent.
- Tried against a Wazuh 4.9.2 manager and agent: the address was dropped with iptables on the
  agent, and Wazuh removed the rule when the timeout ran out.

## CrowdSec

With a CrowdSec Local API (LAPI), approved blocks reach every bouncer of that LAPI (firewall, nginx,
Cloudflare), and Wolf and CrowdSec share detections. Off by default; runs every minute on the
central site only.

::steps{level="3"}
### Create the credentials

```bash [CrowdSec host]
cscli bouncers add dodock-wolf   # prints the bouncer key: decisions in
cscli machines add dodock-wolf --password '<long random password>'  # detections and blocks out
```

### Fill Wolf Settings → CrowdSec

| Setting                                                                      | Default | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Use CrowdSec**                                                             | off     | turns the integration on                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Local API URL**, **Bouncer API key**, **Machine ID**, **Machine password** |         | the LAPI and the credentials above                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Send detections**                                                          | on      | security events with an IP, at or above **Minimum severity sent** (`warning`), become LAPI alerts with the scenario `dodock-wolf/<category>`. Past events are not replayed.                               |
| **Let CrowdSec decide on detections**                                        | off     | off: alerts carry `remediation: false`, CrowdSec records them (`cscli alerts list`) and decides nothing. On: CrowdSec's profiles decide; the default profile bans the IP for 4 h, with no human approval. |
| **Apply approved blocks**                                                    | on      | an approved **Block IP** goes to the LAPI as a `ban` decision for the approved duration (origin `dodock-wolf`).                                                                                           |
::

**Decisions in**: Wolf reads the LAPI's decisions (the whole list on the first run and every hour,
the changes in between), including CrowdSec's own detections, `cscli` bans and the community
blocklist when the LAPI is enrolled. A security event whose IP is under a decision gets
`payload.crowdsec` (type, origin, scenario, until) and one severity step more. Wolf's own blocks are
tagged but not raised.

The agent still applies its own block when its responder is on, and the incident comment says what
was sent where. Tested against CrowdSec 1.6.4.


# Alert rules

A **Wolf Alert Rule** reads a window of metrics or events every minute. When its condition holds, it
opens one incident per group and notifies its channels.

## Fields

| Field                                                                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Signal Type**                                                        | `metric`: aggregate metric samples (or their rollups for windows over 3 h, see [Metric storage](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/metric-storage)). `event`: count Wolf Events. `sequence`: an event followed by another on the same IP, user or host, see [Sequence rules](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#sequence-rules). |
| **Metric Name** / **Event Type**, **Event Category**, **Min Severity** | What to read. For example `http_502`, or `security` / `web_attack_probe`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Aggregation**                                                        | `avg`, `min`, `max`, `sum`, `count`, `last`. Use `min` for "stayed above for Z minutes" and `sum` for counters such as `http_5xx`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Operator**, **Threshold**                                            | `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `==`, `!=` against a number.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Window Minutes**                                                     | The look-back. Default 5.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Min Samples**                                                        | Fewer samples in the window than this, and the rule does not breach.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Group By**                                                           | `host`, `bench`, `site`, `host_label` (for example per disk mount) or `none`. One incident per group.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Filter Host / Bench / Site**                                         | Limit the rule to one scope.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Active From / To**                                                   | Only evaluate in this window. It may wrap midnight (`04:00 → 01:00`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Require Recent Deployment**                                          | Only fire if a deployment hit the same bench, site or host in the last **Deployment Window Minutes** (30).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Fire / Resolve After Evaluations**                                   | Consecutive breached (or clear) evaluations, one per scheduler tick, before an incident opens (or auto-resolves). Default 1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Separate Resolve Threshold**                                         | Hysteresis: fire above 90, resolve only once at or below 80.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Cooldown Minutes**                                                   | Re-fire into the just-resolved incident instead of opening a new one. An event rule reopens it only for an event newer than the resolution; a metric rule, while its window still breaches. Default 30.                                                                                                                                           |
| **Auto Resolve**                                                       | Resolve the incident when the condition clears. Default on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Channels**                                                           | Where alerts go. See [Channels](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/channels).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Notify On Resolve**                                                  | Also tell the channels when the incident resolves, automatically or by hand. Default on. PagerDuty always hears it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Escalate After Minutes**, **Escalation Channels**                    | If still `Open` (not acknowledged) this long after the first alert, notify the escalation channels once.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Severity**                                                           | Of the incident: `info`, `warning`, `critical`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

The rule form shows **Last Evaluated**, **Last Fired** and **Last Error**.

## Examples

::tabs
  :::tabs-item{label="502 spike"}
  | Field               | Value      |
  | ------------------- | ---------- |
  | Signal Type         | `metric`   |
  | Metric Name         | `http_502` |
  | Aggregation         | `sum`      |
  | Operator, Threshold | `>=`, `10` |
  | Window Minutes      | `5`        |
  | Group By            | `site`     |

  *10 or more 502 responses on a site within 5 minutes.*
  :::

  :::tabs-item{label="Disk stayed full"}
  | Field                      | Value               |
  | -------------------------- | ------------------- |
  | Signal Type                | `metric`            |
  | Metric Name                | `disk_used_percent` |
  | Aggregation                | `min`               |
  | Operator, Threshold        | `>`, `90`           |
  | Window Minutes             | `15`                |
  | Group By                   | `host_label`        |
  | Separate Resolve Threshold | `80`                |

  *Every sample of a mount above 90 % for 15 minutes. Resolves at or below 80 %.*
  :::

  :::tabs-item{label="Night cron"}
  | Field               | Value             |
  | ------------------- | ----------------- |
  | Signal Type         | `event`           |
  | Event Type          | `cron_failure`    |
  | Aggregation         | `count`           |
  | Operator, Threshold | `>=`, `1`         |
  | Window Minutes      | `10`              |
  | Group By            | `site`            |
  | Active From / To    | `01:00` → `04:00` |

  *Any failed scheduled job between 01:00 and 04:00.*
  :::
::

## Sequence rules

A rule of type `sequence` fires when an event of one list of categories follows an event of another
on the same entity. For example: a web probe, then an SSH login from the same address within the hour.

| Field                        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **First Event Categories**   | Categories of the first event, one per line, for example `web_attack_probe`.                                                                                                       |
| **First Event Min Severity** | Only first events at or above this severity. The scope filters apply to the second event.                                                                                          |
| **Then Event Categories**    | Categories of the event that must follow, one per line.                                                                                                                            |
| **Same**                     | `ip`: the second event's remote address (`payload.ip`), public only. `user`: the same user on the same site. `host`: the same host under any of its names (**Wolf Entity Alias**). |
| **Within Minutes**           | The longest gap between the two events. Default 60.                                                                                                                                |

- The threshold counts the second events seen in the window.
- There is one incident per entity value (`ip 203.0.113.5`), scoped like its newest second event.
- The gap runs from the first event's last occurrence to the second's latest, so repeats folded into
  one record count. A brute force of thousands of first events is one candidate.
- The incident links both events. An event already in another incident stays there, and the
  incident's timeline, which starts at the first event, shows it anyway.

Three [presets](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/presets#sequences-across-sources) use it.

## Maintenance windows

A **Wolf Silence** (host, bench, site and/or rule, **Starts At**, **Ends At**) keeps incidents
opening, so the timeline stays complete, but holds back their notifications. Incidents still open
when the window ends are notified then.

Create one:

- in Desk (**Wolf Silence → New**);
- through the REST API: `POST /api/resource/Wolf Silence`;
- with the deployment marker: `wolf-agent mark-deployment --bench main --silence 15m`.

## Digests

Each channel row can use an **hourly digest**: `info` and `warning` alerts are batched into one
message per destination. `critical` alerts are always sent at once, and PagerDuty is never
digested.

## Test a rule

**Send test notification** on the rule form sends a TEST to every enabled channel row and shows
what each one answered.

## Rules as YAML

Alert rules can live in a file: in git, reviewed in a pull request, copied from one Wolf site to another.

```bash
bench --site wolf.example.com wolf-rules export -o rules.yaml           # every rule; --rule NAME for some
bench --site wolf.example.com wolf-rules import rules.yaml              # what it would change
bench --site wolf.example.com wolf-rules import rules.yaml --apply      # write it
```

In Desk, the **Wolf Alert Rule** list's menu has **Export to YAML** (the selected rules, or all) and **Import from YAML**, which previews first and applies only after a second click. Both need the Wolf Manager or System Manager role.

```yaml [rules.yaml]
version: 1
rules:
- rule_name: Disk almost full
  enabled: 1
  severity: critical
  metric_name: disk_used_percent
  aggregation: min
  threshold: 90
  group_by: host_label
  channels:
  - channel_type: ntfy
    ntfy_server: https://ntfy.example.com
    ntfy_topic: ops
```

- **Field names** are the rule form's own. A rule lists only what differs from the defaults, and on import **a field the file leaves out goes back to its default**: the file says all of a rule.
- **Matched by `rule_name`**: a new name creates a rule, an existing one is updated. Rules not in the file are left alone.
- **Secrets are never written**: chat webhook URLs, tokens, the PagerDuty routing key, the SMS secret, every password field. A file that holds one is refused, to keep them out of git. A generic Webhook's URL and an SMS auth header template are not secret fields: they are exported.
- **Channels keep their stored secrets.** On import a channel matches the existing row of its type with the same settings (Email recipients, ntfy server and topic, Matrix room, SMS URL and numbers…). Slack, Mattermost and PagerDuty rows have nothing but their secret to tell them apart: they match by position, and only when the file keeps as many of them. A channel that matches nothing is new: when it needs a secret it comes in disabled, to set it in the form and then enable it.
- **Nothing half-applied**: an unknown field (a typo), a value the field cannot take (a Select option it does not have, a number that is not one), a rule the form would refuse or a name used twice makes the import apply nothing, and says which rule and why.
- **Quote times**: `active_from: '22:00'`. YAML reads an unquoted `22:00` as a number, and the import refuses it.
- The evaluator's own state (last evaluation, last fired, hysteresis counters) is never exported nor imported.


# Preset rules

Presets are created on install and on each migrate. Edit or disable them freely: they are never
overwritten. They are flagged **Dokos preset** on the rule. Read each condition as the rule's
aggregation over its window, checked every minute.

::warning
Presets have no channels. They open incidents but notify nobody until you add a
[channel](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/channels).
::

## Web and deployments

| Preset                     | Fires when                                         | Per    | Severity   |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------- |
| 502 spike after deployment | `sum(http_502)` >= 10 in 5 min, after a deployment | `site` | ● critical |
| 5xx spike                  | `sum(http_5xx)` >= 25 in 5 min                     | `site` | ● critical |

## Cron, scheduler and workers

| Preset                             | Fires when                                                      | Per          | Severity   |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ---------- |
| Nightly cron failure (01:00-04:00) | `cron_failure` events >= 1 in 15 min, 01:00–04:00               | `site`       | ● critical |
| Scheduler failure                  | `cron_failure` events >= 1 in 15 min, 04:00–01:00               | `site`       | ◐ warning  |
| Scheduler stalled                  | `host_metric_alert` / `scheduler_stalled` events >= 1 in 15 min | `site`       | ● critical |
| Worker crash                       | `worker_failure` events >= 1 in 10 min                          | `bench`      | ● critical |
| Worker queue backlog               | `min(queue_length)` > 500 in 10 min                             | `host_label` | ◐ warning  |
| Background jobs failing            | `sum(rq_failed_jobs_added)` >= 5 in 10 min                      | `bench`      | ◐ warning  |
| Long-running background job        | `min(rq_long_running_jobs)` > 0 in 15 min                       | `host_label` | ◐ warning  |
| No background workers              | `max(rq_workers)` < 1 in 5 min                                  | `bench`      | ● critical |
| Queue Redis memory high            | `min(redis_used_memory_percent)` > 90 in 10 min                 | `bench`      | ◐ warning  |
| Queue Redis evicting keys          | `sum(redis_evicted_keys)` >= 1 in 10 min                        | `bench`      | ● critical |
| Bench process down                 | `min(bench_processes_down)` > 0 in 3 min                        | `bench`      | ● critical |

## Hosts and agents

| Preset             | Fires when                                                 | Per          | Severity   |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ---------- |
| Disk almost full   | `min(disk_used_percent)` > 90 in 5 min                     | `host_label` | ● critical |
| High CPU           | `min(cpu_usage)` > 90 in 10 min                            | `host`       | ◐ warning  |
| High memory        | `min(memory_used_percent)` > 90 in 10 min                  | `host`       | ◐ warning  |
| High load          | `avg(load_per_core)` > 2 in 10 min                         | `host`       | ◐ warning  |
| Agent silent       | `host_metric_alert` / `agent_silent` events >= 1 in 15 min | `host`       | ◐ warning  |
| Host setup problem | `last(agent_setup_failed)` >= 1 in 120 min                 | `host`       | ◐ warning  |

## Backups, TLS, database and email

| Preset                                  | Fires when                                            | Per          | Severity   |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ---------- |
| No backup for 26 h                      | `last(backup_age_hours)` > 26 in 60 min               | `site`       | ◐ warning  |
| Backup failed                           | `error` / `backup_failed` events >= 1 in 60 min       | `site`       | ● critical |
| TLS certificate expiring within 14 days | `last(tls_days_left)` < 14 in 180 min                 | `host_label` | ◐ warning  |
| TLS certificate expiring within 3 days  | `last(tls_days_left)` < 3 in 180 min                  | `host_label` | ● critical |
| Database connections high               | `min(db_connections_used_percent)` > 85 in 5 min      | `host_label` | ◐ warning  |
| Slow queries                            | `sum(db_slow_queries)` >= 20 in 10 min                | `host_label` | ◐ warning  |
| Replication lag                         | `min(db_replication_lag_seconds)` > 300 in 10 min     | `host_label` | ● critical |
| Replication stopped                     | `max(db_replication_running)` < 1 in 5 min            | `host_label` | ● critical |
| Email queue backlog                     | `error` / `email_queue_backlog` events >= 1 in 15 min | `site`       | ◐ warning  |
| Email sending errors                    | `error` / `email_queue_error` events >= 1 in 15 min   | `site`       | ◐ warning  |

## Logins and accounts

| Preset                        | Fires when                                                    | Per    | Severity   |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------- |
| SSH brute force               | `security` / `ssh_failed_login` events >= 20 in 10 min        | `host` | ● critical |
| SSH login after brute force   | `security` / `ssh_login_after_failures` events >= 1 in 10 min | `host` | ● critical |
| Repeated sudo failures        | `security` / `sudo_failure` events >= 3 in 10 min             | `host` | ◐ warning  |
| New system account            | `security` / `account_created` events >= 1 in 10 min          | `host` | ◐ warning  |
| User added to admin group     | `security` / `admin_group_change` events >= 1 in 10 min       | `host` | ● critical |
| Repeated failed Frappe logins | `security` / `frappe_failed_login` events >= 5 in 10 min      | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| Admin login from new IP       | `security` / `new_admin_ip` events >= 1 in 10 min             | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| Admin login from new country  | `security` / `admin_login_new_country` events >= 1 in 10 min  | `site` | ● critical |
| Privileged role granted       | `security` / `privileged_user` events >= 1 in 10 min          | `site` | ● critical |

## Attacks and intrusion

| Preset                                  | Fires when                                                          | Per     | Severity   |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------- |
| Web attack scan                         | `security` / `web_attack_probe` events >= 100 in 10 min             | `site`  | ◐ warning  |
| Sensitive file served                   | `security` / `web_sensitive_file_exposed` events >= 1 in 10 min     | `site`  | ● critical |
| Network IDS alert (critical)            | `security` / `network_ids_alert` events (critical) >= 1 in 10 min   | `host`  | ● critical |
| Host intrusion alert (critical)         | `security` / `hids_alert` events (critical) >= 1 in 10 min          | `host`  | ● critical |
| Honeytoken touched                      | `security` / `honeytoken_triggered` events >= 1 in 10 min           | `site`  | ● critical |
| Bench service exposed                   | `last(exposed_services)` > 0 in 30 min                              | `host`  | ● critical |
| Development settings in production      | `last(site_config_risks)` > 0 in 30 min                             | `site`  | ◐ warning  |
| Bench code changed outside a deployment | `security` / `bench_code_changed` events (critical) >= 1 in 30 min  | `bench` | ● critical |
| Bench or server config changed          | `security` / `bench_config_changed` events (warning) >= 1 in 30 min | `host`  | ◐ warning  |
| Bench connects somewhere new            | `security` / `bench_new_outbound` events (warning) >= 1 in 15 min   | `host`  | ◐ warning  |

## Application changes and posture

| Preset                         | Fires when                                                      | Per    | Severity   |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------- |
| Server Script can run new code | `security` / `server_script_change` events >= 1 in 10 min       | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| Client Script can run new code | `security` / `client_script_change` events >= 1 in 10 min       | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| System Console used            | `security` / `console_execution` events >= 1 in 10 min          | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| Security settings weakened     | `security` / `security_settings_weakened` events >= 1 in 10 min | `site` | ● critical |
| Permission rules changed       | `security` / `permission_change` events >= 1 in 10 min          | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| API key generated              | `security` / `api_key_generated` events >= 1 in 10 min          | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| API key used from a new IP     | `security` / `api_key_new_ip` events >= 1 in 10 min             | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| Webhook to a new host          | `security` / `webhook_external` events >= 1 in 10 min           | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| Unusual data export            | `security` / `data_exfiltration` events >= 1 in 60 min          | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| Security score low             | `last(security_score)` < 60 in 180 min                          | `site` | ◐ warning  |
| Regulatory deadline            | `security` / `regulatory_deadline` events >= 1 in 15 min        | `site` | ● critical |

## Sequences across sources

| Preset                                  | Fires when                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Per    | Severity   |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
| Scan then login from the same IP        | one of `web_attack_probe`, `network_ids_alert`, then one of `ssh_login_after_failures`, `ssh_root_login`, `new_admin_ip`, `admin_login_new_country`, `api_key_new_ip` on the same `ip` within 60 min                                                                                 | `ip`   | ● critical |
| New-IP login then export or new key     | one of `new_admin_ip`, `admin_login_new_country`, `api_key_new_ip`, then one of `data_exfiltration`, `api_key_generated`, `webhook_external` on the same `user` within 120 min                                                                                                       | `user` | ● critical |
| IDS alert then risky change on the host | one of `network_ids_alert`, `hids_alert` (critical), then one of `server_script_change`, `client_script_change`, `console_execution`, `permission_change`, `security_settings_weakened`, `privileged_user`, `api_key_generated`, `webhook_external` on the same `host` within 60 min | `host` | ● critical |

**Per** is the rule's **Group By**: one incident per site, bench, host or `host_label` (a disk mount,
a queue, a domain). For a [sequence rule](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/rules#sequence-rules) it is the entity: one incident
per IP, user or host. The conditions are those of a fresh install, generated from
[`dodock_wolf/wolf/presets.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/dodock_wolf/wolf/presets.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}
by `docs-site/scripts/presets-table.py`. See [Security](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security) for the signals behind the
security presets.


# Channels

Each row of a rule's **Channels** (or **Escalation Channels**) table is one destination. Secrets
(tokens, keys, webhook URLs) are Password fields: stored encrypted, never logged, and scrubbed from
every recorded error.

**Send test notification** on the rule form sends a TEST to every enabled row and shows what each
one answered.

## Types

| Type       | Sends                                                                                                  | Settings                                                                             |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Email      | one email per recipient, with signed Acknowledge / Resolve links                                       | Recipients                                                                           |
| Webhook    | generic JSON `{text, incident}` ([protocol](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/protocol)) | Webhook URL                                                                          |
| Raven      | a message in a Raven channel                                                                           | Raven Channel                                                                        |
| Slack      | Block Kit message with a severity colour bar and Open / Acknowledge / Resolve buttons                  | Incoming Webhook URL\*                                                               |
| Mattermost | message attachment with colour, fields and Acknowledge / Resolve links                                 | Incoming Webhook URL\*                                                               |
| Matrix     | `m.room.message` with an HTML body                                                                     | Homeserver URL, Room ID, Access Token\*                                              |
| ntfy       | push with title, priority, tags, click and action buttons                                              | Server URL (default ntfy.sh), Topic, Access Token\* (optional)                       |
| Gotify     | push with priority mapped from severity and a click URL                                                | Server URL, Application Token\*                                                      |
| SMS        | short text (one or two SMS) through any HTTP gateway                                                   | Phone Numbers, Gateway URL template, Method, Body, Auth Header, Secret\*, Max Length |
| PagerDuty  | Events API v2: trigger, acknowledge, resolve; `dedup_key` = incident name                              | Routing Key\*, Events API URL                                                        |

\* Password field: stored encrypted, shown as asterisks.

## Who hears what

- Opened and reopened incidents go to the **Channels**; escalations to the **Escalation Channels**.
- When someone acknowledges or resolves an incident (Desk or a signed link), **PagerDuty** channels
  always get the matching `acknowledge` / `resolve` event, so the alert closes on call too.
- The other channels hear a resolution only when the rule has **Notify On Resolve**.
- A test from the rule form triggers then resolves on PagerDuty, so it never leaves an alert open.
- With an **hourly digest** on a row, `info` and `warning` alerts are batched into one message per
  destination. `critical` alerts are always immediate. PagerDuty is never digested.
- During a [maintenance window](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/rules#maintenance-windows), notifications wait until it ends.

## Signed action links

Alerts for unresolved incidents carry signed **Acknowledge** / **Resolve** links, valid 24 h
(**Wolf Settings → Action Link Hours**). Opening a link shows a confirmation page; only its button
acts, so mail scanners cannot acknowledge for you. Security incidents also carry a link per
[response action](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/response-actions) Wolf proposes; those ask for a Wolf Manager's login.

## Delivery status

Every attempt is recorded as a **Wolf Delivery**: channel, target without secrets, kind, PagerDuty
action, ok or error, HTTP status. The incident lists them under **Deliveries**. Deliveries follow
the event retention.

## Setup per type

::collapsible{name="Slack"}
Create an app → **Incoming Webhooks** → **Add New Webhook to Workspace**, and paste the
`https://hooks.slack.com/services/…` URL. Buttons open the incident or the signed action page, so no
Slack interactivity endpoint is needed. Slack may show a warning icon on link buttons of apps
without one.
::

::collapsible{name="Mattermost"}
**Integrations → Incoming Webhooks → Add**, and paste the `https://…/hooks/…` URL.
::

::collapsible{name="Matrix"}
Create a bot account, invite it to the room and join. Get its access token (Element: **Settings →
Help & About → Access Token**, or `POST /_matrix/client/v3/login`). The Room ID is the internal
`!…:server` one (**Room settings → Advanced**), not an alias. Messages are sent with
`PUT /_matrix/client/v3/rooms/{room}/send/…`.
::

::collapsible{name="ntfy"}
Any topic on ntfy.sh or your own server. On a public server, pick an unguessable topic, or protect it
and paste an access token (`tk_…`). Priority: critical 5, warning 4, info 3, resolved 2; escalations
one step higher.
::

::collapsible{name="Gotify"}
**Apps → Create application**, and paste its token. Priority: critical 8, warning 5, info 3,
resolved 2; escalations two steps higher.
::

::collapsible{name="SMS"}
Provider agnostic. The Gateway URL and the optional Body Template take `{to}`, `{text}` and
`{secret}` placeholders: URL-encoded in the URL and form bodies, JSON-escaped in JSON bodies. The Auth
Header is a header line such as `Authorization: Bearer {secret}`. Put API keys in **Secret**, never
in the URL. One request per phone number.

The text (kind, severity, title, scope, and the incident URL when it fits) is folded to the GSM-7
alphabet and cut on a word boundary to 160 characters (one SMS) or 306 (two). Text that needs
Unicode fits 70 / 134.

```text [A gateway that takes JSON]
Gateway URL:   https://sms.example.com/api/send
Method / Body: POST, json, {"to": "{to}", "message": "{text}"}
Auth Header:   Authorization: Bearer {secret}
```
::

::collapsible{name="PagerDuty"}
Add an **Events API v2** integration to a service and paste its integration key as the Routing Key.
Change the Events API URL for the EU region (`https://events.eu.pagerduty.com/v2/enqueue`), or for an
Events-v2 compatible receiver: Grafana OnCall, Opsgenie and others accept the same body.
::


# Incidents

A **Wolf Incident** groups the events of one rule for one group (a site, bench, host or label). It
is `Open`, then `Acknowledged`, then `Resolved`. Rules with **Auto Resolve** close it when the
condition clears; a person can acknowledge or resolve it at any time, from the Wolf UI, Desk or a
signed link in the alert.

:screenshot{alt="A resolved incident in the Wolf UI" caption="A resolved incident: timeline with the deployment, the events, comments and status changes." name="incident-resolved"}

## The timeline

The incident's timeline interleaves its events with comments, assignments and status changes: who
acknowledged or resolved it (from Version history), and auto-resolves (from the incident's own
fields).

**Evidence** is what the incident's rule matched: the events of an event rule, both events of a
sequence rule, and for a metric rule its summary and the events behind the metric (the 502
responses of `http_502`). Evidence is what the event count, Merge, Split and the proposed
[response actions](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/response-actions) work on.

The timeline also shows every other event of the incident's scope (site, bench, host) in its window,
whatever the source, as **context**, and the deployment that preceded it. Sharing a site, bench or
host alone never makes an event evidence: a 502 on a site does not belong to the site's *Server
Script can run new code* incident. When the incident took events from other scopes (by
IP or user, or through a sequence rule), it shows the deployments and health events of those scopes
too: a Suricata alert on the database host comes with that host's deployment and failed crons, not
the Error Logs of every site it serves. Each user sees only the scopes they may read.

## Grouping by IP or user

A security event joins the open incident that holds an event naming the same IP or user, seen
within **Entity Correlation Minutes** (60), whatever its source, host, bench or site. A Suricata scan
on one host, a Wazuh SSH alert on another and a web probe on a site, all from one address, read as
one incident.

- Only a public remote address (`payload.ip`) counts. A server's own address, private, loopback and
  documentation ranges would tie unrelated attacks together.
- A user ties events only when it is an e-mail address (`root` on two hosts or `Administrator` on
  two sites are not one person), and not from failed logins or `sudo` failures, whose user the
  attacker chose.
- Only incidents started in the last 24 hours take events by entity, so a scanner coming back every
  hour does not keep one incident growing.
- A rule's evidence is its own: when a rule fires on events another incident took by IP, they move
  to the rule's incident.
- It works both ways. When a rule opens or reopens an incident, the incident also takes the security
  events already stored that share an IP or user with its evidence and that no incident holds yet,
  with the same bounds: from **Entity Correlation Minutes** before the evidence to 5 minutes after,
  no info events, not for an incident started over 24 hours ago. The incident then starts at the
  earliest of them. nginx, Suricata and Wazuh report one attack within seconds, while rules run
  every minute: without this, the events that arrived first would stay out.
- An event that joined by IP or user is marked **Joined by IP or User**. A rule that matches it
  later takes it back for its own incident; an event a person moved (merge, split) stays put.

Both settings are in **Wolf Settings → Correlation**. Untick **Group Incidents by IP or User** (on by
default) and events become evidence only of the rules that match them.

Each event says who raised it: the Wolf agent, the Wolf site, Suricata or Wazuh. An event that is
the [same finding](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/wazuh-suricata#both-one-finding-two-sources) as another source's says
"same finding as …" and links to that row when it is on the page.

## Working an incident

Wolf Managers can:

- **Assign to me**, or set **Assigned To**. Frappe's assignment runs (ToDo, sidebar, notification to
  the assignee), and the sidebar's own assign and unassign keep the field in step.
- **Add comment** on the timeline. Wolf Users can comment too.
- Take a [response action](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/response-actions) on a security incident.

### Manual incidents

Create one in Desk, or use **Open incident from this event** on a Wolf Event. Manual incidents have
no rule, so the rules engine never auto-resolves them.

### Merge and split

- **Merge into…** (Desk: **Actions**; Wolf UI: **Merge…**) moves events and comments to the target
  and resolves the source with **Merged Into** set. If the source came from a rule, further
  breaches of that rule feed the target instead of opening a duplicate.
- **Split…** moves the events you tick to a new incident (no rule, **Split From** set).
