```json [health]
             "ingest_queue": "short", "ingest_backlog_seconds": null}
}
```

| Field                           | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rules.last_evaluated`          | Latest `last_evaluated` over enabled **Wolf Alert Rules** (the rule engine runs at each scheduler tick); `null` if no rule ran yet.                                                                                 |
| `scheduler.enabled` / `reason`  | `false` with `maintenance_mode`, `pause_scheduler`, `disable_scheduler` or `enable_scheduler unset in System Settings`.                                                                                             |
| `scheduler.last_job_run`        | Latest `Scheduled Job Type.last_execution`, stamped when a worker starts a job.                                                                                                                                     |
| `scheduler.tick_seconds`        | Seconds between Frappe scheduler ticks, so between two rule evaluations: 240 on Frappe 15 and Dodock unless `scheduler_tick_interval` is set; `null` on a Frappe without the setting. Informative, never a problem. |
| `*.age_seconds`                 | Server-side `now - timestamp`, so agent clock skew does not matter. **Negative** when the stored time lies in the future, which happens after a system time-zone change and stalls the scheduler until that time.   |
| `queues`                        | RQ queue lengths and worker count for the bench, or `{"error": "..."}` if Redis is unreachable.                                                                                                                     |
| `queues.ingest_backlog_seconds` | How long the oldest job of the ingest queue (`ingest_queue`) has waited; `null` when it is empty. Queued pushes are answered before they are stored, so this is the only sign that telemetry is not arriving.       |
| `ok` / `problems`               | The server's own reading, with a 5 minute threshold.                                                                                                                                                                |

Two things are problems:

- **staleness**: `abs(age) >= stale threshold` on `rules`, or on `scheduler` when no rule is
  enabled;
- **ingest backlog**: `ingest_backlog_seconds >= stale threshold`.

Scheduler and queue state are context appended to the staleness text. The agent applies its own
threshold (`watchdog.stale_minutes`) to the raw ages rather than trusting `ok`.

While rules are stale, each push also records a `host_metric_alert` / `scheduler_stalled` event
on the site, bumped rather than duplicated for 15 minutes. The **Scheduler stalled** preset turns
it into an incident once the scheduler runs again. A stalled site cannot alert about itself, so
the live alert is raised by the agent watchdog through its own fallback channel (see
[Watchdog](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/watchdog)).

## Wazuh integration

```http [POST /api/method/dodock_wolf.api.wazuh.alert]
POST /api/method/dodock_wolf.api.wazuh.alert
X-Wolf-Agent-Id: WAG-0005
X-Wolf-Agent-Secret: <secret>
Content-Type: application/json

<one Wazuh alert, as Wazuh writes it in alerts.json>
```

| Aspect          | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Credentials     | A **Wolf Agent** registered with `"kind": "integration"`, through the same [registration](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#registration). It is never reported silent, since it only pushes when Wazuh has an alert.                           |
| What Wolf keeps | The alert becomes a `hids_alert` event, mapped like the agent's `alerts.json` reader. The `dodock_wolf` group (Wazuh's alerts on Wolf's own export) and the `sca` group are not stored, and the answer says why: `{"stored": false, "reason": ...}`. |
| Repeats         | The same rule and subject within 10 minutes bump the event's count.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Rate limit      | Up to 600 calls a minute per integration.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Sender          | [`agent/wazuh/custom-dodock-wolf`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/agent/wazuh/custom-dodock-wolf){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, the script Wazuh's integration daemon runs.                                                         |

See [Wazuh and Suricata](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/wazuh-suricata).

## Incident action links

Email, Raven and webhook alerts for unresolved incidents carry signed links:

```http [GET /api/method/dodock_wolf.api.actions.incident_action]
GET /api/method/dodock_wolf.api.actions.incident_action
    ?incident=WINC-00012&action=ack|resolve&expires=<unix seconds>[&actor=<email>]&sig=<hex>
```

| Parameter  | Meaning                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `incident` | The **Wolf Incident**.                                                                                                                  |
| `action`   | `ack` or `resolve`.                                                                                                                     |
| `expires`  | Unix seconds.                                                                                                                           |
| `actor`    | The recipient's address in emails (one email per recipient). Absent for Raven and webhooks.                                             |
| `sig`      | HMAC-SHA256 over `wolf-incident-action\n<incident>\n<action>\n<expires>\n<actor>`, with a key derived from the site's `encryption_key`. |

Links expire after **Wolf Settings → Action Link Hours** (default 24, `0` disables them).

GET only renders a confirmation page. Its button POSTs the same parameters, and only the POST
acknowledges or resolves, so link scanners cannot act on an incident. The incident records
`acknowledged_by` / `resolved_by` as the logged-in user, else the `actor`, else `link`.

Where the links appear:

| Channel             | Form                                                                       |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Webhook             | `incident.actions = {"ack": "...", "resolve": "..."}`, empty once resolved |
| Slack               | Block Kit buttons                                                          |
| Mattermost          | Attachment links                                                           |
| ntfy                | `Actions` header                                                           |
| Matrix, Gotify, SMS | Incident URL only                                                          |

Hourly digests are posted to webhooks as:

```json [Digest webhook body]
{"text": "...", "digest": [{"incident", "kind", "severity", "title", "at", "url"}]}
```

### Response links

One link per action Wolf proposes on the incident, up to 5:

```http [GET /api/method/dodock_wolf.api.actions.response_action]
GET /api/method/dodock_wolf.api.actions.response_action
    ?incident=WINC-00012&action=block_ip|disable_user|logout_sessions|revoke_api_keys&target=<ip or user>
    [&agent=<Wolf Agent>&hours=<1..168>]&expires=<unix seconds>[&actor=<email>]&sig=<hex>
```

`sig` is HMAC-SHA256 over
`wolf-response-action\n<incident>\n<action>\n<target>\n<agent>\n<hours>\n<expires>\n<actor>`
with the same key.

::caution
Only a logged-in Wolf Manager or System Manager can confirm (POST), through the Response panel's
rules.
::

| Channel                                                | Form                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| Email (one per recipient), Raven, Matrix, Gotify, ntfy | Links in the text and HTML of the alert   |
| Webhook                                                | `incident.responses = [{"label", "url"}]` |
| Slack                                                  | Buttons                                   |
| Mattermost                                             | Links                                     |
| SMS                                                    | None                                      |

## Native channels

Each native channel is a pure builder in
[`dodock_wolf/wolf/channels/`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/dodock_wolf/wolf/channels/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}
that maps a notification to the documented format of the service. The module docstrings cite the
reference pages. See [Channels](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/alerts/channels) for setup.

| Channel    | Request                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Slack      | `POST <webhook>` `{"text", "attachments": [{"color", "fallback", "blocks": [section, actions]}]}`                                                                                                                                          |
| Mattermost | `POST <webhook>` `{"attachments": [{"fallback", "color", "pretext", "title", "title_link", "text", "fields", "footer"}]}`                                                                                                                  |
| Matrix     | `PUT <homeserver>/_matrix/client/v3/rooms/<room>/send/m.room.message/wolf-<attempt>` (Bearer token) `{"msgtype": "m.text", "body", "format": "org.matrix.custom.html", "formatted_body"}`                                                  |
| ntfy       | `POST <server>/<topic>`, body = text, headers `Title` (RFC 2047 when not ASCII), `Priority`, `Tags`, `Click`, `Actions`, optional `Authorization: Bearer`                                                                                  |
| Gotify     | `POST <server>/message` (`X-Gotify-Key`) `{"title", "message", "priority", "extras": {"client::display", "client::notification": {"click": {"url"}}}}`                                                                                     |
| SMS        | The configured template, one request per number                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| PagerDuty  | `POST <events url>` `{"routing_key", "event_action", "dedup_key": "<incident>", "payload": {"summary", "source", "severity", "component", "group", "class", "custom_details"}, "client", "client_url", "links"}` (payload on trigger only) |

PagerDuty event actions:

| Wolf notification                | `event_action`            |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `fired`, `reopened`, `escalated` | `trigger`                 |
| Acknowledgement                  | `acknowledge`             |
| Resolution                       | `resolve`                 |
| Test                             | `trigger`, then `resolve` |

### Wolf Delivery

Every request is recorded as a **Wolf Delivery**:

| Field                      | Meaning                                                            |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `incident`, `alert_rule`   | What was notified.                                                 |
| `at`                       | When.                                                              |
| `channel_type`             | Slack, Matrix, PagerDuty…                                          |
| `target`                   | The destination without secrets: host, room, masked phone numbers. |
| `kind`, `action`, `digest` | What was sent.                                                     |
| `ok`, `http_status`        | The result.                                                        |
| `error`                    | The error, with secrets and URL paths and queries removed.         |

Digests of native channels are merged on a SHA-256 of the channel settings, and the digest item
keeps a reference to the channel row rather than any secret.


# UI API

These are the APIs behind the Wolf UI (`/wolf`,
[#19](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/issues/19){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}). They need the Wolf User, Wolf Manager or
System Manager role, and apply the caller's access rules inside the query (see
[Access](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/access)). Answers are not cached per user, so each one is the caller's own;
two reads share a short cache filtered per caller (see [Short cache](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#short-cache)).

| Area                                                                                | Methods                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Overview](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#overview)                         | `scope.get_counts`, `scope.get_inventory`                                                               |
| [Incident page](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#incident-page)               | `incident_view.list_incidents`, `get_incident`, `get_timeline`, `act`, `merge_preview`, `split_preview` |
| [Dashboards](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#dashboards)                     | `dashboard.get_signals`, `get_http`, `get_monitoring`                                                   |
| [Explorers](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#explorers)                       | `explore.list_events`, `list_error_groups`, `get_error_group`                                           |
| [Metrics explorer](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#metrics-explorer)         | `metrics.get_metric_catalog`, `query_metric`                                                            |
| [Security](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#security)                         | `security.list_sites`, `get_posture`                                                                    |
| [Regulatory reporting](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#regulatory-reporting) | `compliance.get_report`                                                                                 |
| [Response actions](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#response-actions)         | `response.get_response`, `approve`                                                                      |

Every method is under `dodock_wolf.api.`, for example `/api/method/dodock_wolf.api.scope.get_counts`.

## Common arguments

### Time window

| Argument         | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `range`          | Relative window ending now: a number and `m`, `h` or `d`, such as `15m`, `24h`, `7d`. Default `24h`.                                                                                                                        |
| `since`, `until` | Explicit window, ISO 8601. A time without an offset is read as UTC, as in the [agent protocol](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/protocol). `until` defaults to now and needs `since`. They win over `range`. |

- A relative window is measured in real time: across a DST change, `24h` is 24 hours, not 23 or
  25 hours of wall clock.
- Windows longer than 400 days, or with `since` after `until`, are refused.
- The Desk overview APIs (`api/ui.py`) accept the same `range` values.

Every response that reads a window returns what it actually read, in UTC:

```json [window]
"window": {"since": "2026-10-29T13:00:00Z", "until": "2026-10-30T13:00:00Z", "relative": "24h", "time_zone": "Europe/Paris"}
```

`time_zone` is the site's. Stored times are in that zone. The UI converts with it, never with the
browser's zone.

In the Wolf UI, the window is in the URL (`?range=7d` or `?since=…&until=…`). A range selected on
the HTTP chart of a dashboard, or on the chart of the metrics explorer, becomes an explicit
`since`/`until`: the dashboard's counts and chart, and the event and error explorers opened from
it, are read with it. **Back to a relative window** drops it.

### Scope

`site`, `bench` and `host` narrow a query to records with those values.

::warning
**`bench` needs `host`.** Bench names such as `frappe-bench` repeat across hosts, so a bench alone
is ambiguous and refused.
::

### Access

A restricted Wolf User, one with **Wolf User Scope** rows, gets counts and inventory over the
records they may see, and `"restricted": true`.

::note
A Wolf User **without any** Wolf User Scope row is not restricted: they see everything, as in
Desk. That is the current rule, kept as is.
::

## Overview

### `dodock_wolf.api.scope.get_counts`

Exact counts for the overview and entity dashboards. Arguments: window and scope.

```json [get_counts]
{
  "window": {...},
  "scope": {"host": "bench-01"},
  "restricted": false,
  "incidents": {
    "unresolved": 60, "unacknowledged": 40, "critical_unresolved": 7,
    "by_status": {"Open": 40, "Acknowledged": 20},
    "by_severity": {"info": 0, "warning": 53, "critical": 7},
    "sites_with_unresolved": 1, "unresolved_without_site": 5,
    "opened_in_window": 61, "resolved_in_window": 1,
    "basis": "..."
  },
  "events": {"records": 12, "occurrences": 140, "by_type": {"error": {"records": 3, "occurrences": 90, "by_severity": {...}}}, "basis": "..."},
  "agents": {"agent": {"fresh": 3, "stale": 1, "never_seen": 0, "disabled": 0}, "satellite": {...}, "silence_minutes": 5, "basis": "..."}
}
```

| Part        | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `incidents` | `unresolved` counts Open and Acknowledged incidents now, whatever the window. `unacknowledged` is Open only. Merged incidents are excluded. `unresolved_without_site` counts host- or bench-wide incidents, which have no site. `opened_in_window` and `resolved_in_window` use `started_at` and `resolved_at`.    |
| `events`    | `records` are Wolf Events first seen in the window. `occurrences` sums their reported `count`. A deduplicated record keeps counting repeats, including repeats after the window, so `occurrences` is not a count of occurrences inside the window.                                                                 |
| `agents`    | Agents are hosts, so `site` and `bench` do not filter them. A satellite is not a host and is counted apart; with `host`, it counts when one of its registered benches runs on that host. `fresh` means seen within the agent silence threshold of Wolf Settings, the same rule as the Desk overview's online flag. |

### `dodock_wolf.api.scope.get_inventory`

The hosts, benches and sites the caller may see. Argument: `days`, the telemetry window
(default 7, at most 90).

```json [get_inventory]
{
  "hosts": [
    {"host": "bench-01", "sources": ["agent", "events", "metrics"], "last_seen": "2026-10-30T12:59:30Z",
     "benches": [{"bench": "frappe-bench", "host": "bench-01", "sources": [...], "last_seen": "...",
                  "sites": [{"site": "a.example.com", "sources": [...], "last_seen": "..."}]}],
     "sites": []}
  ],
  "unplaced_sites": [],
  "note": "Hosts and benches come from agent registrations and from telemetry in the window. ...",
  "days": 7,
  "restricted": false,
  "as_of": "2026-10-30T13:00:02Z"
}
```

`as_of` is when the registrations and telemetry were read: they are cached for a few seconds (see
[Short cache](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#short-cache)).

| Source               | Meaning                                                                              |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `agent`, `satellite` | What an agent declared when it registered.                                           |
| `events`             | By when they last happened, so a recurring deduplicated event keeps its site listed. |
| `metrics`            | Rollups.                                                                             |
| `incidents`          | Unresolved ones, whatever their age.                                                 |

A registration names every site of a bench; a restricted user sees only the granted ones.
Neither kind of source is complete on its own: a bench added after its agent registered appears
once it sends telemetry, and a quiet site only through its agent's registration. The UI shows
`sources` and `note` rather than presenting the list as complete.

- A bench is always under its host.
- `host.sites` holds sites seen on a host whose bench is unknown.
- `unplaced_sites` holds sites seen without a host, for example a satellite with no host
  information. They are not attached to a guessed host.
- Times are UTC.

## Incident page

### `dodock_wolf.api.incident_view.list_incidents`

Incidents the caller may see, newest first.

| Argument                | Meaning                                      |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `status`                | `unresolved` (default), `resolved` or `all`. |
| `site`, `bench`, `host` | Scope.                                       |
| `limit`                 | At most 200.                                 |
| `cursor`                | Continues a page.                            |

Pages follow `(started_at, name)`, so two incidents started at the same second are neither
repeated nor skipped. Returns `incidents`, `paging` (`has_more`, `next_cursor`) and `time_zone`.

### `dodock_wolf.api.incident_view.get_incident`

The incident header in one call: title, status, severity, scope, start, acknowledgement,
resolution and owner, rule, silence, notification and escalation times, merge and split links,
and the timeline window.

| Field               | Meaning                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `deployment`        | Time of the deployment before the incident, with `available: false` when retention deleted its event but the incident kept the time. |
| `event_records`     | Linked Wolf Events. `event_count` is the same number, as on **Wolf Incident**.                                                       |
| `event_occurrences` | The occurrences they report, repeats included. A different number from `event_records`.                                              |
| `can`               | Which actions the caller may take.                                                                                                   |
| `regulatory`        | See [Regulatory reporting](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#regulatory-reporting).                                             |

Wolf Users read and comment. Wolf Managers also acknowledge, resolve, take the incident, and:

- `merge`: the incident is not merged;
- `split`: not merged, and at least two events are linked (one must stay);
- `postmortem`: not merged, and either resolved or already has one (`postmortem` names it).

Each matches the check the action itself makes.

### `dodock_wolf.api.incident_view.get_timeline`

One page of the timeline, oldest first.

| Argument   | Meaning                                       |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `incident` | The **Wolf Incident**.                        |
| `limit`    | Default 100, at most 500.                     |
| `cursor`   | Continues a page.                             |
| `families` | Comma-separated subset of the families below. |

| Family     | Rows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `evidence` | Wolf Events linked to the incident, at any time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `context`  | Other events in its scope (site, the same bench on the same host, or host-wide) during its window, if the caller may see them, and the deployment before it even when that is older than the window. When the incident took events from other scopes (by IP or user, or a sequence rule), also the deployments and health events (`error`, `cron_failure`, `worker_failure`, `host_metric_alert`) of those scopes in the window: of the site; of the bench on its host; on a host, its host-wide events and its benches' deployments and failed crons and workers, not its sites' Error Logs. At most 10 such scopes, the same on every page. An incident with no site, bench or host has only that second kind, in Desk too. A user who may read one of those scopes but not the event that brought it in can still tell, from its rows, that the incident reached it. |
| `activity` | Status changes, assignments, comments and notes, from Frappe's Version and Comment history.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `delivery` | Notification attempts (**Wolf Delivery**).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Each row has a stable `id`, `family`, `kind`, `at` (UTC) and a plain-text `summary`. Ids:
`event:<name>`, `activity:comment:<name>`, `activity:version:<name>:<field>`,
`delivery:<name>`, `deployment:<incident>`.

Per kind:

| Kind       | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Events     | `relation`: `linked`, `context` or `preceding_change` (the deployment before the incident, never called its cause). `count`, `first_seen` and `last_seen` describe a deduplicated record: one row, not one row per occurrence. `details` is the event payload, for display as text. `source_label` says who raised it (`Wolf agent`, `Wolf site`, `Suricata`, `Wazuh`). `duplicate_of` names another source's event about the same finding, seen first ([overlapping detectors](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/wazuh-suricata#when-detectors-overlap) in `both` mode); its row id is `event:<duplicate_of>`. |
| Activity   | `user_name`. Comments and notes come as plain `text`, never HTML to render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Deliveries | `channel`, `action`, `target`, `result` and `http_status`. `result` is `accepted` when the endpoint took the message, which does not mean a person read it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

- Rows are ordered by time, then events, activity and deliveries, then id. Rows with the same
  time have no causal order.
- `paging.next_cursor` continues after the last row. The same rows come back once each,
  whatever the page size.
- Activity keeps the newest 200 recorded changes and 300 comments.
  `truncated.activity_version` and `truncated.activity_comment` report when older ones exist.
- `window` is the incident's window: start minus `padding_minutes`, to its resolution or now. It
  is the same window Desk and the postmortem use.

### `dodock_wolf.api.incident_view.act`

POST `incident` and `action`, one of `acknowledge`, `resolve` or `assign_to_me`. It runs the
incident's own method, so Frappe's write permission applies, and returns the new
`get_incident`.

The incident's state is checked first:

- acknowledging needs an Open incident;
- resolving or taking needs an unresolved one;
- merged incidents refuse every action.

A page left open on a stale incident gets an error instead of reopening it.

### `dodock_wolf.api.incident_view.merge_preview`

Arguments: `source`, and optionally `target`. Wolf Managers with write permission only. Nothing is
written.

- `candidates`: where the source may go. These are unresolved, unmerged incidents the caller may
  read: the newest 50 (`more_candidates` says when there are more), the source's site first,
  then its bench.
- `preview`, for a `target`:
  - `error`: the merge's own refusal (itself, a merged incident, no write permission) or `null`;
  - the `events` and `comments` that would move;
  - `target_after`: severity, start and status, once the target covers both;
  - `source_after`: Resolved, merged into the target.

The merge itself is `dodock_wolf.api.incident.merge` (POST `source`, `target`), which checks
again.

### `dodock_wolf.api.incident_view.split_preview`

Arguments: `incident`, and optionally `events` (a JSON list of Wolf Event names). Wolf Managers
only. Nothing is written.

- `events`: the linked events, oldest first, at most 500 (`more_events`).
- `preview`, for a selection:
  - `error`: the split's own refusal (nothing ticked, an event not linked, all of them ticked)
    or `null`;
  - `moved` and `kept`;
  - `new_incident`: title, severity, start and status. It is Open, or Resolved when the source
    is. It has no alert rule, so nothing resolves it by itself.

The split itself is `dodock_wolf.api.incident.split` (POST `incident`, `events`, `title`). The
postmortem is created by `dodock_wolf.api.incident.create_postmortem` and edited in Desk.

## Dashboards

### `dodock_wolf.api.dashboard.get_signals`

The newest value of every signal series in scope (`site`, `bench` with `host`, `host`): one series
per metric, host, bench, site and label. Each series has a `state`:

| State       | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `firing`    | An enabled rule on this metric applies to the series and has an open incident for its scope and, for rules grouped by label, its label (`incidents`). A firing series whose samples stopped stays firing, with `stale: true`.                                                  |
| `stale`     | Samples stopped: none in the last 2 hours, or none for three collection intervals, at least 5 minutes (backups: 30 min). The old value is not presented as current. The cadences are the agent's defaults: an agent set to probe TLS or backups less often looks stale sooner. |
| `watched`   | Rules apply (`rules`: aggregation, operator, threshold, window) and none has an open incident.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `unwatched` | A value, but no rule watches it. The dashboard does not invent a threshold.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

| Field     | Meaning                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `missing` | Signals with no series at all in the last 7 days: not collected for this scope, not set up, or not available here. They are never shown as zero.           |
| `counts`  | Exact states per group, whatever the 300-series limit.                                                                                                     |
| `email`   | Email queue problems the site recorded about itself in the last 24 hours.                                                                                  |
| `as_of`   | When the series were read (see [Short cache](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#short-cache)). Rules, incidents and states are read with each request. |

A restricted user sees what each rule checks, but not the host, bench or site filters it names.
The metric meanings (unit, kind, cadence) are in
[`wolf/catalog.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/dodock_wolf/wolf/catalog.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

### Short cache

`get_inventory` and `get_signals`, the overview's two slow reads, keep what they read for
`wolf_read_cache_seconds`: site config, default `30` (an agent's push interval), `0` turns it off.
`get_inventory` caches its registrations and telemetry triples, `get_signals` its series (newest
value and last time seen).

::caution
The cached value is read **without** access conditions and is the same for every caller. Each
request then keeps the rows its caller may see, by the rule of
[`wolf/scopes.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/dodock_wolf/wolf/scopes.py){rel=""nofollow""}. A
cached value never carries one user's grants to another.
::

- Rules, open incidents and the email queue are read per request: a signal's state follows an
  incident at once.
- A value is **fresh** for `wolf_read_cache_seconds`. Older, and up to 4 times that (2 min by
  default), it is still served at once, and one background job (deduplicated, `short` queue)
  reads it again. Older still, or missing, the request reads.
- Between visits, the scheduler reads again, every minute, the values asked for in the last 10
  minutes (10 at most per site) that are no longer fresh (`read_cache.refresh_active`). It needs
  `scheduler_tick_interval` at 60 (see [Install the Wolf App](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/wolf-app)): at Dodock's
  default 4 min tick, a visit after 2 quiet minutes reads.
- A series that starts, or a value that changes, shows up a minute or two later at most. `as_of`
  says when the data was read. A [live update](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#live-updates) refetches, and may get the cached
  value.
- A change of `wolf_read_cache_seconds` takes effect within a minute: Dodock's web workers keep
  the site config in memory for up to 60 s.
- There is one cached value per site and per scope (`get_signals`' site, bench and host; the
  inventory's `days`): a dashboard of another scope has its own.

Measured effect: [Performance](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/performance#the-short-cache).

### `dodock_wolf.api.dashboard.get_http`

Requests, 5xx and 502 per bucket over the window. Arguments: the common window and scope
arguments.

- Values are summed across labels and read at the resolution of the window (`resolution`).
- Only whole buckets are read (`window`; `requested_window` is what was asked): the bucket still
  filling shows once it closes, instead of drawing a drop in traffic.
- 502 is part of 5xx and is never added to it.
- A bucket without samples is `null`: a gap, not a zero. `has_data` tells "no data" from "zero".
- `deployments` lists the deployments in the requested window. On a site's dashboard that
  includes deployments recorded for its whole bench (no site), as incidents link them.

### `dodock_wolf.api.dashboard.get_monitoring`

Whether Wolf itself works: the site's health (rules, scheduler, ingest queue), rollup watermarks,
every agent and satellite with its state, last contact, clock skew and version, its `setup` (the
agent's last `wolf-agent doctor` run: `checked_at`, `failed`, `warnings`, and the `problems` with
their fix), and this site's mode. Each part is reported on its own.

::note
An online agent says nothing about its watchdog's fallback channel.
::

## Explorers

Wolf Events are deduplicated: one record holds its first time (`first_seen`), last time
(`last_seen`) and the number of repeats it absorbed (`count`). Explorer lists are lists of
records. They never say how many times something happened inside a window when a record spans
the window's edge, and each response says so in `basis`.

Searches (`q`) match a plain substring of the title, at most 100 characters: `%` and `_` match
themselves, and there is no regex.

### `dodock_wolf.api.explore.list_events`

Event records active in the window (first seen before its end, last seen after its start), newest
first, paged by `(first seen, name)`.

| Argument                             | Meaning                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `range`, `since`, `until`            | Window.                                   |
| `site`, `bench`, `host`              | Scope.                                    |
| `event_type`, `severity`, `category` | Filters.                                  |
| `q`                                  | Title substring.                          |
| `limit`                              | At most 200.                              |
| `cursor`                             | Continues a page.                         |
| `entity`                             | Security events naming an entity (below). |

Payloads are not in the list: `get_event(name)` returns one record with its payload.

`entity` keeps the security events of every source (Wolf, Suricata, Wazuh) that name it:
`ip:203.0.113.5`, `host:erp-01`, `site:erp.example.com` or `user:jane@example.com`. Values are
normalised and resolved through the aliases. For example, `host:erp-01` also finds the Wazuh
alerts of the agent named `wazuh-erp01` when an alias says they are the same host.
`dodock_wolf.api.entities.find(entity, ...)` is the same list. The response echoes `entity`.

### `dodock_wolf.api.explore.list_error_groups`

Groups of error records, by fingerprint, that have a record active in the window, latest first.
The window and `q` choose the groups. Their figures cover every record of the group the caller
may see, whatever its age, as on the group's page, so a recurring error is not presented as new:

- `records`, and `records_in_window`;
- `occurrences`, the sum of the records' counts;
- `first_seen` and `last_seen`;
- the number of `sites`, and whether some records are host-wide;
- the number of linked `incidents`;
- the title of the most recently seen record, which stands for the group.

A fingerprint includes the site unless the agent sends its own, so most groups concern one site.

### `dodock_wolf.api.explore.get_error_group`

Every visible record of one group, whatever its age:

- where it happened, by site, bench and host;
- the incidents it is linked to that the caller may read (`incidents_not_visible` counts the
  others);
- its most recently seen record with the payload: the representative traceback, the same record
  the list shows;
- its 50 most recently seen records.

A restricted user sees only the records of their sites, benches or hosts, and counts over those.

## Metrics explorer

### `dodock_wolf.api.metrics.get_metric_catalog`

Every catalogued metric
([`wolf/catalog.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/dodock_wolf/wolf/catalog.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"})
and the custom metrics seen in the last 7 days. Each one has:

| Field                       | Meaning                                              |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `kind`, `unit`              | What the value is.                                   |
| `level`                     | `host`, `bench` or `site`.                           |
| `label_key`                 | `mount`, `queue`, `domain`, `db`, `of` or `manager`. |
| `aggregations`, `group_bys` | What it allows.                                      |
| `seen`                      | Whether the caller has data for it.                  |

- Gauges are read as `avg`, `min`, `max` or `last`.
- Interval counts are read as `sum` (the total per bucket), `avg` or `max` (per push interval).
- A custom metric is read as a level.
- Grouping follows the metric's level: a host metric has no bench or site. Metrics with a label
  also group by `host_label`, and so may a custom metric, whose labels the catalog cannot name.

The catalog lists every metric the agent sends, which a unit test checks against the agent's
source. `get_labels(metric, scope)` lists a metric's label values (at most 100), including those
first seen in the last hour.

### `dodock_wolf.api.metrics.query_metric`

| Argument         | Meaning               |
| ---------------- | --------------------- |
| `metric`         | Metric name.          |
| `aggregation`    | Default per kind.     |
| `group_by`       | Default `none`.       |
| `label`          | Label value.          |
| window and scope | The common arguments. |

A combination the catalog does not allow is refused: a sum of disk levels, the last value of an
interval count, a host metric grouped by site.

The answer reads whole buckets (`bucket_seconds`; `window` is what was read, `requested_window`
what was asked) at a resolution fine enough for the window's length that still reaches back to
its start (`resolution`). A two-hour zoom into last week reads minute rollups, because raw
samples that old are purged (see [Metric storage](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/metric-storage)). It is exact across
raw samples and rollups. Groups are ranked in SQL first, and only the shown ones are read per
bucket.

Each of `series` has:

| Field                    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `points`                 | One per bucket, `null` for a bucket without samples (a gap, not a zero).                                                                                                                                |
| `value`                  | The aggregation over the whole window.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `samples`, `last_sample` | Sample count and newest sample.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `stale`                  | Judged only when the window reaches now (`live`), and from the newest sample, not the last whole bucket (which lags by up to a bucket). In a past window the last sample is just where the window ends. |

`groups` says how many groups exist and which `MAX_GROUPS` (20) are shown, ranked by the
aggregation, highest first (lowest for `min`). `retention.clipped` is true when the window starts
before the data kept at this resolution (`kept_from`, the cutoff purge applies): those buckets
are gaps.

## Live updates

The Wolf UI stays current over Frappe's own socket.io server
([`dodock_wolf/wolf/live.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/dodock_wolf/wolf/live.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"},
[`frontend/src/services/live.js`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/frontend/src/services/live.js){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}).
The server never pushes telemetry. It sends an **invalidation**, the event `wolf_invalidate`, and
the page fetches again through the APIs above, which check permissions as usual.

| Room                       | Joined with         | Frappe checks                                              | Message                                      |
| -------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `doc:Wolf Incident/<name>` | `doc_subscribe`     | read permission on that incident (Wolf User Scope applies) | `{"kind": "incident", "incident": "<name>"}` |
| `doctype:Wolf Incident`    | `doctype_subscribe` | read permission on the DocType                             | `{"kind": "incidents"}`                      |
| `doctype:Wolf Event`       | `doctype_subscribe` | read permission on the DocType                             | `{"kind": "events"}`                         |

- **Sent when**: an incident is created, saved, updated by the engine (new linked events, reopen,
  auto-resolve, silence, escalation, assignment, postmortem) or deleted; a comment on an incident
  is added, edited or deleted; a delivery is recorded; an event is stored.
- **At most one message per room and transaction**, after commit. The bookkeeping is cleared on
  commit and on rollback, so a job that commits many times announces each transaction and a
  rolled-back one announces nothing. List messages are also throttled to one per 5 s per kind.
  One held back is marked after commit and sent by `flush_live_updates` (every minute): a
  committed change can be delayed, never lost.
- **No names in list rooms**: a restricted reader only learns that something changed somewhere.
- **Boot**: `capabilities.realtime` gives `namespace` (`/<site>`), `port` (`socketio_port`, for
  `bench start`), `dev_server` and `poll_seconds`. Behind nginx the socket uses the site's own
  origin (`/socket.io` is proxied, as for Desk).

What each page does with a message:

| Page                    | On a message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Without a socket                        |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Incident                | Header refreshed. New timeline rows are added without scrolling, and a "N new rows: show" button takes the reader to the first one. Loaded rows and expanded rows stay. Past 500 loaded rows only the header follows and the rows wait for Refresh. | Polls every 60 s                        |
| Incidents               | Refreshed, unless "Load more" was used: then "Incidents changed · Refresh".                                                                                                                                                                         | Polls, same rule                        |
| Overview and dashboards | Refreshed at most every 10 s (messages carry no scope; relative windows move). Also polled every 60 s while live, because metrics are not announced.                                                                                                | Polls                                   |
| Events, Errors          | Never reshuffled under the reader: "New events recorded · Refresh" (the new events may not match the filters).                                                                                                                                      | Not polled: "Not live: refresh by hand" |

- Every page reconciles once when the socket first joins its rooms (what changed after its first
  fetch is unknown) and after each reconnect (messages sent while offline are lost).
- A page that does not reload by itself shows "Reconnected, changes may have been missed ·
  Refresh" after a reconnect. A poll or the first connect never claims a change.
- **Pause** holds messages, and the page says changes are waiting, until **Resume**.
- Every refresh, the reader's included, goes through one queue: never two at once.
- Polling skips hidden tabs.

## Security

### `dodock_wolf.api.security.list_sites`

Sites with a recent `site_config_risks` or `backup_age_hours` sample, plus the Wolf site itself
(not on a satellite), filtered by the caller's access.

### `dodock_wolf.api.security.get_posture`

Argument: `site` (default: the Wolf site). A site the caller may not see is a 403.

| Field                                     | Meaning                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `site`                                    | The site.                                                                                 |
| `local`                                   | The Wolf site: its System Settings are readable.                                          |
| `hosts`                                   | Hosts of the site.                                                                        |
| `recent_hours`                            | Agent samples older than this (3) are not used.                                           |
| `score`                                   | Weight passed over total weight. An unknown check counts as not passed.                   |
| `coverage`, `passed`, `failed`, `unknown` | Check totals.                                                                             |
| `checks`                                  | `{id, label, weight, status, evidence, fix}`, `status` being `pass`, `fail` or `unknown`. |

The hourly `record_security_scores` job stores the score as the `security_score` metric. See
[Security](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security).

## Regulatory reporting

`get_incident` returns `regulatory`: `null` when neither flag is set, else
`{nis2, gdpr, reference, deadlines}`. Each deadline is
`{id, regime, label, due_at, done_at, status, estimated}`.

| `status`    | Meaning                  |
| ----------- | ------------------------ |
| `open`      | Not done, not due soon.  |
| `due_soon`  | Due within 6 h.          |
| `overdue`   | Past due.                |
| `done`      | Done in time.            |
| `done_late` | Done after the deadline. |

### `dodock_wolf.api.compliance.get_report`

Argument: `incident`. Returns `{incident, markdown}`: a draft with the facts, the deadlines, the
timeline (linked events and comments, 100 each at most) and the postmortem's impact, root cause,
lessons and action items. Read permission on the incident is enough. Nothing is sent. See
[Compliance](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/security/compliance).

## Response actions

### `dodock_wolf.api.response.get_response`

Argument: `incident`.

| Field                        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `proposals`                  | `{action, target, agent, host, bench, site, reason, label, executors}`, from the incident's security events, without the ones already approved or applied. A block names the attacked `host`, its Wolf Agent in `agent` when it applies it, and `executors` (`wolf_agent`, `wazuh`). |
| `actions`                    | The incident's **Wolf Response Action** rows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `can_approve`                | Whether the caller may approve.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `default_hours`, `max_hours` | Block durations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

### `dodock_wolf.api.response.approve`

POST. Wolf Manager or System Manager only.

| Argument         | Meaning                                                                                          |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `incident`       | The **Wolf Incident**.                                                                           |
| `action`         | `block_ip`, `disable_user`, `logout_sessions` or `revoke_api_keys`.                              |
| `target`         | IP or user.                                                                                      |
| `host`           | For `block_ip`: the attacked host, as proposed.                                                  |
| `agent`          | For `block_ip`, instead of `host` (older links and pages): the Wolf Agent that applies it.       |
| `duration_hours` | For `block_ip`: 1 to 168, for the Wolf Agent's block. A Wazuh block lasts its command's timeout. |
| `reason`         | Free text.                                                                                       |

Refused targets are a validation error, and nothing is recorded: a private or reserved address,
Administrator, Guest, yourself.

Returns the **Wolf Response Action**. User actions come back `Applied` or `Failed`. Blocks stay
`Approved` until the agent reports (see [protocol](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/protocol#response-actions) and
[Response actions](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/response-actions)).


# Metric storage

At 50 hosts × 15 metrics every 30 s, raw samples are about 2 M rows a day. Wolf therefore keeps
three resolutions, each with its own retention in **Wolf Settings → Retention**.

## Resolutions

| Resolution       | DocType                                | Default retention | Read by                                    |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Raw samples      | Wolf Metric Sample                     | 48 hours          | Rule windows up to 3 h, the 1 h chart      |
| 1-minute rollups | Wolf Metric Rollup (`resolution` 60)   | 30 days           | Windows up to 2 days (6 h and 24 h charts) |
| 1-hour rollups   | Wolf Metric Rollup (`resolution` 3600) | 365 days          | Longer windows (7 d chart)                 |

A rollup row stores, for one series (metric, host, bench, site, labels) in one bucket:

- count;
- sum;
- min;
- max;
- the last value, with its time.

So `avg`, `min`, `max`, `sum`, `count` and `last` over whole buckets equal the raw answer.

A read takes, in order:

1. the coarsest resolution allowed for its window, up to the last rolled bucket;
2. then finer rollups;
3. then the raw samples not rolled up yet, so the newest minutes are always there.

A long window loses at most one bucket at its start: under a minute for 1-minute reads, under an
hour for 1-hour reads.

## Rollups

The `rollup_metrics` job runs every minute.

- It rolls closed minutes, 2 minutes after they end, and closed hours.
- Its progress is in **Wolf Rollup State**.
- It recomputes whole buckets, so running it again never double counts.
- Samples that arrive late, for example an agent replaying its spool, move the progress back.
  Their buckets are rolled again, up to the raw retention.

::tip
Rollups, like alert rules, depend on the scheduler tick. Set `scheduler_tick_interval` to 60 (see
[Install the Wolf App](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/install/wolf-app)).
::

## Purge

`purge_metrics` runs hourly and applies the retention.

::note
It never deletes raw samples or 1-minute rollups that are not rolled up yet.
::

Event retention (`event_retention_days`) is separate and unchanged by metric retention.

## Ingest mode

Set in **Wolf Settings → Agents → Ingest Mode**.

| Mode              | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `async` (default) | Validates a push, queues the inserts on the `short` queue and answers at once. A worker inserts the batch and attaches its events to open incidents. If the queue is unreachable, the push is stored inline. |
| `sync`            | Stores during the request.                                                                                                                                                                                   |

In both modes, the agent's last seen time, clock skew and Wolf's health are updated during the
request. The answer an agent gets in each mode is in the
[protocol](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/protocol#ingest-mode).

## Performance

Metric rows are stored in metric and time order, and reads of known metrics scan the primary key
by name range. Measured results at 100 hosts × 7 days are in
[Performance](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/performance).

## Optional time-series backend

::warning
Design only, **not built**.
::

The read path goes through two functions:

- `rollups.aggregate()`, for rules;
- `rollups.series_rows()`, for charts.

Writes go through `events.insert_metrics()`.

A ClickHouse or TimescaleDB backend would implement those three:

| Part                    | ClickHouse                                                                                | TimescaleDB                             |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Raw samples             | A `MergeTree` table                                                                       | A hypertable                            |
| Minute and hour rollups | Materialized views (`AggregatingMergeTree` with `sumState/minState/maxState/argMaxState`) | Continuous aggregates with `first/last` |
| Retention               | TTL                                                                                       | `add_retention_policy`                  |

The watermark logic and the purge job would then be the database's job. Until a site needs more
than a few hundred hosts, the Frappe tables above are enough and keep Wolf a plain Frappe app.


# Performance

The target is the "done when" of [#10](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/issues/10){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}: a
synthetic load of 100 hosts for 7 days keeps `push` p95 under 200 ms and the overview under 1 s.

It was measured on 2026-11-01, three times:

- first as [#55](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/issues/55){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} found it;
- then after the row order and inventory index of
  [#56](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/issues/56){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"};
- then after [#57](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/issues/57){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} moved the remaining reads
  to SQL (see [What changed](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#what-changed)).

::note
All runs used synthetic data and a demo bench, not production observations.
::

## Summary

| Target                             | Before (#55)                      | Row order (#56)                   | SQL reads (#57)                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `push` p95 under 200 ms            | **Met.** 115 ms over HTTP         | **Met.** 108 ms over HTTP         | **Met.** 20.7 ms server side (HTTP not run again)                                                                                |
| Desk overview under 1 s            | Met, except its 24 h chart: 2.1 s | Met, except its 24 h chart: 1.8 s | **Met.** 0.56 s at most (24 h)                                                                                                   |
| Wolf UI overview under 1 s         | **Not met: 13.8 to 23.8 s**       | **Not met: 1.5 s**                | **Met per read: 0.73 s for the slowest**                                                                                         |
| Wolf UI overview page in a browser |                                   |                                   | Without cache: p50 0.82 to 0.97 s, p95 1.00 to 1.26 s. **With the cache, met: p95 0.61 s; after 45 s or 150 s idle, max 0.65 s** |

The page time runs from navigation start until every panel is drawn, in Chromium on the bench
(see [The page in a browser](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#the-page-in-a-browser)). Without the cache its median is under 1 s,
its p95 is not. With the cache, and with it read again in the background (see
[The short cache](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#the-short-cache)), visits after 45 s and 150 s idle were all served from it.
A visit that still reads takes the time without cache:

- the first of the day;
- a scope nobody opened for 10 min;
- the scheduler at its default 4 min tick.

In short, from the README:

- Push p95 is 108 ms over HTTP.
- Metric rows are stored in metric and time order, and the inventory reads an index alone.
- Reads of known metrics scan the primary key by name range, chart buckets are summed in SQL,
  and the newest value of each series is picked in one pass.
- The Wolf UI overview went from 13 to 24 s down to 1.5 s, then 0.73 s for its slowest read.
- In Chromium, the whole page is drawn in 0.9 to 1.0 s at the median and 1.0 to 1.3 s at p95,
  and in 0.53 s (p95 0.61 s) when the inventory and signals come from their 30 s cache
  (`wolf_read_cache_seconds`, shared by every caller and filtered per caller).
- The cache is read again in the background, so pages opened 45 s or 150 s apart all came from
  it (max 0.65 s), showing data 11 to 51 s old.

## What changed

### Row order and inventory index (#56)

**Row order.** InnoDB stores a table's rows in primary key order, and Frappe's primary key is
`name`.

- Before, metric samples got a random name and rollups a hash of their key. One metric's day
  was spread over the whole table, and each row of a read was a page read of its own.
- Now names start with the resolution, a 6-character hash of the metric and the time, then end
  with a hash of the key
  ([`storage.rollup_name`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/dodock_wolf/wolf/storage.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"},
  `sample_name`). A time range of one metric is read from neighbouring pages.
- Rows are inserted in name order, so InnoDB fills its pages instead of splitting them in the
  middle.

**Inventory index.** `get_inventory` asks which host, bench and site sent anything in a range.

- MariaDB answered through `(resolution, metric_name, bucket_start)`, then fetched every row of
  the range.
- `(resolution, bucket_start, host, bench, site)` answers it from the index alone.
- It replaces `(resolution, bucket_start)`, which it starts with. That index served the rollup
  job and the purge, and still does. `bucket_start` loses its own index too: no read filters it
  without a resolution.

A first try put the full metric name in the row name (61 characters). That made the rollup table
50 % bigger and filled the bench's disk:

- every secondary index entry repeats the primary key;
- rows of one bucket arrived in hash order, so pages split in the middle.

The names are now 33 characters for rollups and 28 for samples, against 32 and 12 before.

| Table (data + indexes) | Before                 | After                             |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Wolf Metric Rollup     | 7.2 GB for 15.2 M rows | 7.3 GB for 15.5 M rows            |
| Wolf Metric Sample     | 2.2 GB for 8.7 M rows  | 3.1 GB for 8.7 M rows (kept 48 h) |

::note
**On an existing site:**

- `bench migrate` creates the index and drops the two it replaces. On 15 M rows, that took
  1.5 min.
- Rows already stored keep their names, so a read speeds up once its window holds only new rows:
  after a day for the 24 h explorer, 7 days for the hourly reads.
::

### SQL reads (#57)

1. **Name ranges.** A read of known metrics scans one primary key range per metric
   ([`rollups.name_passes`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/dodock_wolf/wolf/rollups.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}):
   rows of one metric and resolution sit together in the key since #56, so a window is a stretch
   of it. No row is looked up through a secondary index. Postgres does not store rows in key
   order and keeps one plain read.
2. **Chart buckets in SQL** (`rollups.bucket_cells`). The explorer read one metric's 144 k minute
   rollups twice, for the totals and the chart, and merged them in Python. It now reads one row
   per host and bucket, summed by the database; the totals are the merge of those.
3. **Last values in one pass.** The value at each series' newest time came from a join of the
   rows with their own group-by. On fresh data MariaDB turned that join into a lookup per series,
   each walking all of its metric's minute rollups: `get_signals` took **194 to 233 s** (two
   runs). `row_number()` over each series reads the rows once: 0.62 s.
4. **Host chart index.** `(resolution, host, metric_name, bucket_start)` replaces
   `(resolution, host, bucket_start)`: Desk's host chart reads four metrics of one host, no
   longer all fifteen.

The 194 s were missed at first. #56's "after" reads ran on data 40 to 45 min old, and a later run
on data 85 to 103 min old: `get_signals` reads the last 2 h, so it saw part of its window. One
read of 243 s in that later run, taken for an outlier, was this. Only a full run on fresh data
showed it on every read.

**Rows named before #56.** Their names are 32 hex digits and sort below every new name, outside
the name ranges. While some remain, a second pass reads them (`name < 'g'`), and MariaDB weighs
it against the indexes. Measured with the 153 k minute rollups of one metric's last day renamed
to old names, explorer over 24 h:

| Second pass                                      | Plan                                      | Median   |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `name < 'g'`                                     | primary key, old rows only                | 770 ms   |
| `left(name, 1) < 'g'` (a function: indexes only) | `(resolution, metric_name, bucket_start)` | 1,145 ms |

With millions of old rows, the primary key range would cost more than the index and the optimizer
takes the index. The plain range stays. Old rows go with retention: 30 days for minute rollups,
365 for hour rollups, by default.

## Data and machine

**Data**, written by
[`ci/load_test.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/ci/load_test.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} on a
throwaway site:

- 100 hosts × 15 metrics × 7 days, samples every 30 s;
- raw samples for the last 48 h (8.7 M rows);
- 1-minute and 1-hour rollups before that, then the real rollup job over the raw window (15.3 to
  15.5 M rollups);
- 16,900 events (one per host per hour).

How it compares with a real site:

- Rows are named as the app names them. #55's run named its synthetic rows in sequence, so in
  time order. Only the last 48 h, written by the rollup job, had the scattered layout of a real
  site. A real site was therefore slower than #55 measured, not faster.
- All hosts' samples of one instant go in at once, in name order. Real pushes arrive host by
  host and a little out of time order, so a real sample table is somewhat less dense than this
  one.
- The data end when loading starts, and read windows end when they are read:
  - the full run read 20 to 35 min after the newest data;
  - \#56's "after" reads (`--reads-only`, once the index was in) read 40 to 45 min after it;
  - \#57's run loaded everything again and read straight after, like the first.

  :brBetween the two runs, reads the index does not touch moved by 11 % at most. `--reads-only`
  refuses data over 2 h old.

**Bench**: the
[demo stack](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/dev/demo/README.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} in Docker, on
4 vCPU and 15 GB RAM:

- Dodock 5.18.8;
- gunicorn, 2 workers × 4 threads;
- MariaDB 10.6 with its default 128 MB `innodb_buffer_pool_size`.

Loading took 34 min, down from 75 (#56), then 20 min (#57). The rollup job caught up on 48 h of
raw samples at once in 12.5 min, down from 32, then 9.5 min. A running site never does that.

\#57's numbers were taken before its review fixes. Those keep only the charted groups' buckets in
memory and let `get_http` use name ranges: neither adds a read.

## Results

In milliseconds. Reads: p95 of 10 runs. Pushes: over every timed push.

### Push, server side

`ingest.accept()`, 200 pushes of 15 metrics:

| Mode                       | Before p95 | #56 p95 | #57 p95 |
| -------------------------- | ---------- | ------- | ------- |
| async (validate and queue) | 16.5       | 15.2    | 15.8    |
| store_batch (the worker)   | 9.8        | 11.0    | 10.5    |
| sync                       | 22.6       | 20.1    | 20.7    |

### Push, over HTTP

[`ci/load_http.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/ci/load_http.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}:

- the agent's request with its headers, straight to gunicorn;
- 600 pushes from 100 agents, through 8 connections at once.

|             | Statuses  | p50  | p95   | max   | Throughput   |
| ----------- | --------- | ---- | ----- | ----- | ------------ |
| Before      | 600 × 200 | 64.4 | 114.9 | 170.4 | 116 pushes/s |
| After (#56) | 600 × 200 | 58.0 | 107.9 | 195.3 | 125 pushes/s |

100 hosts every 30 s need 3.3 pushes/s. #57 does not touch the push path; HTTP was not timed
again.

### Desk overview

`ui.get_overview` plus one host chart:

| Range  | 1 h | 6 h | 24 h      | 7 d |
| ------ | --- | --- | --------- | --- |
| Before | 176 | 606 | **2,102** | 240 |
| #56    | 207 | 516 | **1,754** | 214 |
| #57    | 170 | 180 | 559       | 149 |

The 24 h chart reads one host's minute rollups, and the row order keeps a metric together, not a
host: that host's rows are one per page. With the metric in the host index (#57), it fetches the
four charted metrics' rows only.

### Wolf UI overview

`/wolf` sends six reads at once, so a page waits at least for the slowest one:

- the reads were timed one after another;
