- run in parallel, they share the CPU, the disk and the buffer pool, so the page itself is
  slower.

| Read                      | Before               | #56                                  | #57            |
| ------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------- |
| **get_signals**           | **7,971 to 10,569**  | **1,471** (on older data, see above) | 617            |
| **get_inventory**         | **13,836 to 23,799** | 870                                  | 726            |
| get_counts (1 h to 7 d)   | 6.8 to 75.3          | 4.2 to 29.1                          | 3.6 to 40.7    |
| get_http (1 h to 7 d)     | 7.3 to 16.7          | 4.0 to 7.6                           | 4.3 to 11.7    |
| list_incidents            | 0.9 to 4.3           | 1.1                                  | 0.9            |
| get_monitoring            | 11.4 to 15.0         | 41.1                                 | 10.2           |
| **Page, slowest read**    | **13,836 to 23,799** | **1,471**                            | **726**        |
| The six one after another |                      |                                      | 1,359 to 1,398 |

\#55 timed the reads that ignore the range once per range: its ranges there are run-to-run spread.

### The page in a browser

[`frontend/scripts/page-time.mjs`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/frontend/scripts/page-time.mjs){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}
opens `/wolf` in headless Chromium 153, logged in, through the bench's nginx. A page is ready once
its six reads have answered and no panel says it is loading. Two series of 10 runs each:

- cold: a new browser context each time, so the app's scripts and styles are fetched again;
- warm: the same tab navigating again, with its cache.

Two runs, straight after a fresh load of the same data, in ms:

|                                           | Cold p50       | Cold p95           | Warm p50       | Warm p95           |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------ | -------------- | ------------------ |
| **Page ready**                            | **971 to 973** | **1,129 to 1,262** | **887 to 892** | **1,008 to 1,134** |
| App shell (DOMContentLoaded)              | 109            | 134 to 140         | 79 to 85       | 103 to 143         |
| First read sent (app up, session checked) | 211 to 213     | 254 to 262         | 103 to 110     | 130 to 166         |
| Reads, first sent to last answered        | 568 to 569     | 631 to 705         | 586 to 595     | 738 to 801         |
| Drawing, last answer to panels drawn      | 189            | 270                | 120            | 317                |

Where the time goes, at the median of a cold page:

- 0.21 s before the first read: the app's scripts, then its session check.
- 0.57 s of reads. They go out at once and overlap well:
  - `get_inventory`, 0.56 s, and `get_signals`, 0.51 s, set the length;
  - the other four answer in 23 to 62 ms.

  :brIn parallel, each takes about what it takes alone (0.57 s and 0.56 s in-process): the bench's
  two gunicorn workers run them side by side.
- 0.19 s to draw them: the signals table holds its first 300 series, the inventory 101 hosts.

So the p95 goes over 1 s by up to a quarter of a second, in the two slow reads and in drawing.

The demo's nginx serves one site whatever the host name (`wolf.localhost`). The measurement used
a second nginx in the same container, on another port, with the same configuration set to the
load site. A first run through the demo's own nginx timed the demo site, not the load: it is not
counted.

### The short cache

`get_inventory` and `get_signals` keep what they read for 30 s (`wolf_read_cache_seconds`,
[`wolf/read_cache.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/dodock_wolf/wolf/read_cache.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}).
The cached value is read without access conditions, shared by every caller, and each request
keeps what its caller may see (see [UI API](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/ui-api#short-cache)). Rules and incidents
are read per request.

The same page, on one fresh load, in ms:

| `/wolf`, page ready       | Cold p50   | Cold p95       | Warm p50   | Warm p95       |
| ------------------------- | ---------- | -------------- | ---------- | -------------- |
| Cache off (two runs)      | 924 to 955 | 1,134 to 1,169 | 822 to 851 | 1,003 to 1,106 |
| **Served from the cache** | **529**    | **608**        | **280**    | **457**        |

| Served from the cache              | Cold p50 | Warm p50 |
| ---------------------------------- | -------- | -------- |
| First read sent                    | 237      | 91       |
| Reads, first sent to last answered | 62       | 58       |
| `get_inventory` / `get_signals`    | 28 / 59  | 22 / 46  |
| Drawing                            | 228      | 127      |

- With the reads at 60 ms, the page is the app's start (0.1 to 0.25 s) and drawing (0.13 to
  0.23 s at the median, up to 0.32 s).
- In the "served from the cache" runs, every page came within 30 s of a read, so all of them hit.
  How often a real page does depends on how often the overview is opened; at most one visit per
  30 s, per scope, pays the read.
- The second "cache off" run was meant to be a cached one: it started seconds after
  `wolf_read_cache_seconds` was set, and Dodock's web workers keep the site config for up to
  60 s. They still read 0.

#### Read again in the background

A cached value is fresh for 30 s. Up to 2 min old, it is still served at once while one
background job reads it again; and every minute the scheduler reads again the values asked for in
the last 10 minutes. Timed on another fresh load, with the load site's scheduler on and
`scheduler_tick_interval` at 60, one cold page every 45 s, then every 150 s (6 visits each), in
ms:

| `/wolf`, page ready | p50 | p95 | max | `get_inventory` / `get_signals`, p50 |
| ------------------- | --- | --- | --- | ------------------------------------ |
| Every 45 s          | 548 | 649 | 649 | 36 / 78                              |
| Every 150 s         | 563 | 654 | 654 | 49 / 70                              |

- Every visit was served from the cache. At 150 s, past the 2 min a value is kept, only the
  scheduler's read could have kept it: without it, each of those visits would read (0.9 to 1.2 s,
  as without cache).
- The data such a page shows is older. `as_of` sampled 8 times, 40 s apart: 11 to 51 s old, 40 s
  for most. A value read by the scheduler can be up to its minute plus a tick old; at most 2 min,
  after which a request reads.
- A first try of the 45 s series had one 3.2 s page. It came right after `bench clear-cache`, run
  to register the new scheduled job, which empties all of Frappe's cache (its app shell took
  1.8 s): it is not counted. On a site, `bench migrate` registers the job.

#### Drawing the first rows

The signals panel draws the first 10 series of each group, the inventory its first 20 hosts. A
button under each shows the rest, and how many of the hidden series fire or have no new data.
The server sorts problems first, so those are the rows drawn; the counts per group stay exact.

Timed without a bench by
[`frontend/scripts/draw-time.mjs`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/frontend/scripts/draw-time.mjs){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}:
the production build, the API mocked in Chromium with 300 series over 8 groups and 101 hosts of
one bench and two sites each, a new browser context each run, from the last answer to the next
frame. 20 runs, on a laptop, not the bench, in ms:

| Drawing                          | p50            | p95 / max      | List items drawn |
| -------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------- | ---------------- |
| Every row (before)               | 193            | 208            | 503              |
| **First rows** (two series)      | **131 to 134** | **148 to 150** | 121              |
| One series, one host (`--empty`) | 97 to 112      | 126 to 128     | 4                |

The rows cost 80 to 100 ms; 60 ms of it is gone. The rest of the drawing is the page's own, rows
or not.

**The same, on a load bench.** The demo stack (`dev/demo`) on a 16-thread laptop, with a
throwaway site loaded by `ci/load_test.py` (100 hosts × 15 metrics × 7 days: 11.0 M rollups,
8.7 M samples) and a second nginx for it. The overview gets 300 series, all host resources, and
101 hosts. `page-time.mjs`, 10 runs per series, both UI builds swapped into the same containers
and timed twice each, alternating, in ms:

| `/wolf`, p50 (p95) | Cold, page ready            | Cold, drawing           | Warm, page ready         | Warm, drawing           |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------- |
| Every row (before) | 234 to 236 (248 to 258)     | 100 to 103 (115)        | 118 to 126 (129 to 154)  | 48 to 51 (62 to 66)     |
| **First rows**     | **180 to 188 (190 to 206)** | **53 to 55 (56 to 63)** | **80 to 81 (92 to 101)** | **18 to 21 (27 to 30)** |

- Drawing halves cold and drops by 60 % warm: 47 to 50 ms and 27 to 33 ms less. A page opened
  cold is 50 ms faster, a warm one 40 ms.
- Every page was served from the short cache (`get_signals` about 20 ms, `get_inventory` about
  8 ms), so the drawing is what changed; the app's start (first read at 105 to 110 ms cold) did
  not.
- This machine is several times faster than the 4 vCPU bench of the tables above: the uncached
  `get_inventory` took 0.46 s here against 0.73 s there, the whole cached page 0.18 s against
  0.53 s. The bench was not run again; at its speed, the same share of its 0.13 to 0.23 s of
  drawing is about 0.06 to 0.1 s.

### Other reads

| Read                                        | 1 h   | 6 h   | 24 h       | 7 d   |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----- | ---------- | ----- |
| Metrics explorer, cpu_usage by host, before | 1,757 | 7,126 | **25,762** | 2,467 |
| Metrics explorer, #56                       | 219   | 914   | **2,936**  | 506   |
| Metrics explorer, #57                       | 173   | 390   | 863        | 281   |

| Rule query        | Before p95 | #56 p95 | #57 p95 |
| ----------------- | ---------- | ------- | ------- |
| 5 min avg by host | 1.7        | 6.2     | 7.3     |
| 24 h max by host  | **11,355** | 906     | 468     |
| 7 d last by host  | 2,244      | 261     | 67      |

## What is left

Each read is under 1 s, and so is the overview page when its two slow reads come from the cache.

- A visit that reads still takes 0.9 to 1.2 s: the first after 10 quiet minutes on a scope, or
  after 2 minutes when the scheduler ticks every 4 min (Dodock's default; the install sets 60 s).
- Drawing takes 0.13 to 0.32 s on the bench with every row. Drawing the first rows only halves it
  on a faster load bench (100 to 53 ms cold, 50 to 20 ms warm); the rest is the page's own. The
  4 vCPU bench was not run again.
- The metrics explorer over 24 h, 0.86 s, is the closest other read.

These margins are for 100 hosts on this bench. At several times that, the inventory and the 24 h
reads grow with the rows of their window, and so does a visit that reads.

## Not measured

- A user's network: the page was opened on the bench itself, without latency.
- Browsers other than Chromium, and slower machines than this bench's 4 vCPU.
- Rows named before #56 at the scale of an upgraded site: only one metric's day was renamed.
- Postgres. CI installs the app there, which creates the new index, but nothing was timed and the
  upgrade from the old indexes was run on MariaDB only. Postgres stores rows roughly in insertion
  order, which is already time order, so row names matter less there.
- Several sites at once.
- Rule evaluation of every preset at once.
- Disk other than this container's.

## Run it again

::warning
`load_test.py` deletes and rewrites the site's metric tables: never point it at a real site.
::

`ci/load_test.py` fills a throwaway site with N hosts × M metrics × D days and times push and the
overview. CI does not run it. At 100 hosts × 7 days it writes about 20 M rows, which takes 15 to
25 minutes on a GitHub runner before any timing starts. `ci/load_http.py` times the agent's push
over HTTP on the same site.

::steps{level="3"}
### Load and time the reads

On a throwaway site of the bench, from `sites/`:

```bash [sites/]
../env/bin/python /path/to/ci/load_test.py <site> --hosts 100 --metrics 15 --days 7
```

- To time the reads again on the data already loaded, for instance after an index change, add
  `--reads-only`.
- On a site loaded before, empty the three tables first (`truncate`). The script deletes its own
  rows one transaction per table, which on 20 M rows takes long and needs as much undo space.

### Time the push over HTTP

```bash [sites/]
../env/bin/python /path/to/ci/load_http.py <site> --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --agents 100 --pushes 600 --concurrency 8
```

`load_http.py` comes second:

- Its agents report as 100 more hosts (`load-http-NNN`), which the reads would then include. The
  next `load_test.py` run deletes them.
- It raises the site's push limit for the run and puts it back afterwards.
- Its p50 / p95 are over accepted pushes (HTTP 200) only. Every other status or connection error
  is counted separately.

### Time the page in a browser

From `frontend/`, once `yarn install` has run:

```bash [frontend/]
node scripts/page-time.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --site <site> --password <admin password> --runs 10
```

- `--url` is the bench's nginx. It must serve `<site>`: the demo's serves `wolf.localhost` only
  (see [The page in a browser](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/#the-page-in-a-browser)).
- `--path` and `--reads` time another page: its path, and how many Wolf reads it sends.
::

### In the CI container

Add `-e WOLF_LOAD_TEST=1`, and optionally `-e WOLF_LOAD_ARGS="--hosts 20 --days 2"`, to the
`docker run ... integration.sh` command of the [integration job](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/development#integration-job).


# Development

## Status

MVP, tested on a Dokos (Dodock 5.18) bench, on MariaDB 10.6 and on Postgres 17 (see
[`ci/db_smoke.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/ci/db_smoke.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}).

## Live demos

The demo stack in [`dev/demo`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/tree/main/dev/demo){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} runs one
Dokos bench with the Wolf App and its agent. Three profiles add simulated servers, each watched by
an agent of its own; they can run together:

```bash [dev/demo]
WOLF_DEMO_BASE=registry.gitlab.com/dokos/dokos:latest docker compose --profile press --profile multi --profile single up -d --build
docker compose --profile multi logs -f multi-demo   # "history written up to ...", then live
```

| Profile  | Host             | Server                                 |
| -------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `press`  | `f1-demo-press`  | a Press app server, 3 benches, 8 sites |
| `multi`  | `dokos-multi-1`  | plain benches, 2 benches, 6 sites      |
| `single` | `dokos-single-1` | one bench, one site                    |

Each `<kind>-demo` service runs `bench generate-demo-<kind>`: 7 days of history, then an incident
cycle every 30 minutes, with alerts sent to the stack's webhook sink (`docker compose logs catcher`).
[Commands](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/agent/commands) lists what a cycle contains.

### Suricata and Wazuh

The `ids` profile runs a real Suricata (with ET Open) on the bench's network and a real Wazuh
manager reading its nginx log, each with the Wolf agent that reads it. `ids_scenario.py` then sends
one attacker: Wolf's own web detection, Suricata and Wazuh each report it, in one incident.

```bash [dev/demo]
docker compose --profile ids up -d --build
python3 ids_scenario.py
```

## Python tests

```bash [repository root]
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .           # app pure-python tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s agent/tests          # agent tests
```

## Wolf UI

The operator UI at `/wolf` is a Vue app built on [frappe-ui](https://ui.frappe.io){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} in
[`frontend/`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/frontend/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}
([#19](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/issues/19){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}).

- Desk keeps the configuration DocTypes and stays usable for everything the Wolf UI does not show
  yet.
- Its views are added one by one. A view that is not built says so and links to Desk.
- It reuses the Frappe session: guests are sent to the login page, users without the Wolf User or
  Wolf Manager role get a 403.

Screenshots, light and dark, all taken on the demo bench after its 2AM scenario, are in
[`docs/screenshots`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/docs/screenshots/README.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

```bash [frontend/]
cd frontend
yarn install
yarn dev        # Vite on the bench port + 80 (8080 for 8000), proxied to the bench
yarn test       # unit and component tests (Vitest)
yarn build      # writes dodock_wolf/public/frontend and dodock_wolf/www/wolf.html
yarn e2e        # browser tests of that build (Playwright + axe), after `yarn build`
```

::note
Node 20.19 or newer is required. The build output is not committed:
`bench build --app dodock_wolf` produces it on the bench.
::

### Browser tests

The browser tests (`frontend/e2e/`) serve the production build as a bench would
(`e2e/server.mjs`) and answer every API call in the page (`e2e/api.js`), so no Frappe is needed.

Each view must:

- render with no console error and no unanswered call;
- pass axe with no serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA finding, in the light and the dark theme.

Keyboard navigation, reduced motion, acknowledging an incident and where keyboard focus goes are
checked too.

`e2e/states.spec.js` walks every view through loading, empty, filtered-empty, error, forbidden,
partial, stale and disconnected. A view never claims "nothing" before it has read, or after a
read failed, and a refusal says what may not be seen.

The tests need Chromium: run `npx playwright install chromium`, or point `WOLF_CHROMIUM` at an
installed one.

The APIs the UI reads are in [UI API](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/ui-api).

## CI checks

Every pull request and every push to `main` runs
[`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}:

| Job                     | Runs on                      |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Lint (ruff, shellcheck) |                              |
| App tests               | Python 3.12                  |
| Agent tests             | Python 3.9 and 3.14          |
| Wolf UI tests and build | Node 20.19 and 24            |
| Wolf UI browser tests   | Playwright + axe             |
| Bench integration       | MariaDB 10.6 and Postgres 16 |

To run the same checks locally:

```bash [repository root]
pip install ruff==0.17.3                             # ruff rules are in pyproject.toml
ruff check .
shellcheck agent/install.sh ci/integration.sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
python3.9 -m unittest discover -s agent/tests        # the agent must keep working on 3.9
```

### Integration job

The integration job installs this checkout into the public Dokos image, creates a site and runs
[`ci/db_smoke.py`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/ci/db_smoke.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, which
exercises every Wolf SQL path.

::tabs
  :::tabs-item{label="MariaDB"}
  ```bash [repository root]
  docker network create wolf-ci
  docker run -d --name db --network wolf-ci -e MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=admin mariadb:10.6 \
    --character-set-server=utf8mb4 --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
  docker run -d --name redis --network wolf-ci redis:6.2-alpine
  docker run --rm --network wolf-ci --entrypoint bash -v "$PWD:/src:ro" \
    registry.gitlab.com/dokos/dokos:latest /src/ci/integration.sh mariadb
  ```
  :::

  :::tabs-item{label="Postgres"}
  Start `postgres:16` as `db` with `-e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=admin`, and pass `postgres` to
  `integration.sh` instead of `mariadb`. The `redis` container and the network are the same.
  :::

  :::tabs-item{label="Existing bench"}
  ```bash [sites/]
  ../env/bin/python /path/to/ci/db_smoke.py <site>
  ```
  :::
::

To add the load test to the same container run, see
[Performance](https://bthuner.github.io/dodock-wolf/reference/performance#in-the-ci-container).

## This documentation site

The site is Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 + Nuxt Content 3, in `docs-site/`.

```bash [docs-site/]
nvm use            # Node 24 (.nvmrc)
yarn install
yarn dev           # http://localhost:3000, French at /fr
yarn generate      # static site in .output/public
```

- English pages are in `content/en/`, served at `/`. French pages are in `content/fr/`, served at
  `/fr`, with the same file names.
- The number prefix of a file or folder orders pages and is dropped from the URL.
- Every English page has a French twin at the same path, so the language switch lands on the
  same page.

The page map, front matter, components and voice are in
[`docs-site/CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/bthuner/dodock-wolf/blob/main/docs-site/CONTRIBUTING.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.
